job.title: Distribution Associate (QIC - Quality Inventory Control) - 3rd Shift
job.description:
Position: Distribution Associate (QIC - Quality Inventory Control) - 3rd Shift
Location: Rochester, NY

Summary: Nesco Resource is seeking a dependable and detail-oriented Distribution Associate – QIC to join a leading distribution and warehouse operation in Rochester, NY. This temp-to-perm opportunity offers candidates the chance to demonstrate their skills and transition into a permanent position based on performance and business needs. The Distribution Associate will play a key role in inventory control, product replenishment, cycle counting, and warehouse organization while ensuring inventory accuracy and compliance with FIFO requirements. This position is ideal for individuals who enjoy working in a fast-paced warehouse environment, are comfortable using RF scanners and warehouse management systems, and take pride in maintaining accurate inventory records.

Pay Rate:

  • $18.00/Hour
    • + 15% Shift Differential for 3rd Shift

Shift(s):

  • 3rd Shift: 10:00 PM - 6:00 AM | Sunday - Thursday

Job Duties:

  • Perform inventory searches using warehouse management systems (WMS) and RF scanning equipment
  • Organize and maintain picking locations to ensure inventory availability and FIFO compliance
  • Complete product restocking and put-away activities accurately and efficiently
  • Retrieve products to resolve customer order shortages
  • Sort and stage products for proper put-away and storage
  • Conduct product location checks to maintain inventory accuracy
  • Participate in monthly cycle counts and assist with physical inventory activities
  • Follow all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and regulatory requirements
  • Report safety concerns, sanitation issues, equipment malfunctions, and quality concerns to leadership immediately
  • Maintain attendance standards, including working scheduled holidays and overtime when required
  • Support warehouse operations and perform additional duties as assigned

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • Previous warehouse, distribution, or receiving experience preferred
  • Basic math skills required for inventory and cycle counting activities
  • Basic computer proficiency required
  • Experience with warehouse management systems (WMS) preferred
  • Forklift and/or man-up equipment experience preferred
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to follow detailed instructions and adhere to safety procedures
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Reliable attendance and strong work ethic

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to stand for extended periods throughout the shift
  • Frequent walking, bending, stooping, kneeling, squatting, twisting, and pushing/pulling activities
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. regularly throughout the workday
  • Occasional stair climbing and overhead reaching
  • Ability to safely operate man-up equipment as required
  • Comfortable working in a warehouse environment with varying temperatures, noise levels, and dust exposure
  • Ability to work safely around moving mechanical equipment while following all PPE requirements

job.title: Welder
job.description:
Location: Webster, NY
Employment Type: Full-Time | Temp-Hire

Summary: Nesco Resource is seeking skilled and dependable Structural Steel MIG Welders to join our client's manufacturing team in Webster, NY. This direct hire opportunity offers the chance to work in a fast-paced fabrication environment producing high-quality structural steel components. The ideal candidate will have MIG welding experience, the ability to interpret blueprints, and a strong commitment to safety, quality, and craftsmanship.

Pay:

  • $22.00 - $27.00/Hour (Based On Experience)

Schedule:

  • B shift - 3:00 PM - 11:30 PM (Monday - Friday)
    • OT Required, As Needed

Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform MIG welding on structural steel components in accordance with AWS D1.1 welding standards.
  • Prepare materials for fabrication by cutting, grinding, cleaning, fitting, and positioning metal components.
  • Read and interpret blueprints, engineering drawings, work orders, and fabrication specifications.
  • Inspect completed welds to ensure quality, accuracy, and compliance with production standards.
  • Verify measurements, angles, and weld gaps using tape measures, calipers, micrometers, and other precision measuring tools.
  • Operate semi-automatic welding equipment and other fabrication tools safely and efficiently.
  • Grind, repair, and finish welds as needed to meet quality requirements.
  • Operate overhead cranes to safely transport steel materials and completed assemblies throughout the facility.
  • Complete production records and maintain accurate job documentation.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area while following all company safety policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional fabrication and production duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Minimum of one (1) year of MIG welding and metal fabrication experience.
  • Experience welding structural steel preferred.
  • Ability to successfully complete AWS D1.1 Structural Steel Welding certification provided by the client.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, work instructions, and technical drawings.
  • Basic computer proficiency and mechanical aptitude.
  • Strong math skills, including fractions, decimals, and accurate tape measure reading.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Reliable transportation.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to lift and move materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Stand for extended periods throughout the workday.
  • Frequently bend, twist, kneel, crouch, reach, push, and pull while performing fabrication tasks.
  • Ability to safely wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including welding helmet, gloves, hearing protection, safety glasses, flame-resistant clothing, and steel-toed boots.
  • Comfortable working in a manufacturing environment where temperatures may fluctuate with outdoor conditions.
  • Exposure to welding fumes and fabrication equipment in a facility equipped with ventilation systems that meet OSHA standards.

Employee Benefits:

  • Direct Hire opportunity

  • Paid Time Off

job.title: Lead Controls Engineer
job.description:
Lead Engineer Controls:

SUMMARY:
This position's primary responsibility is to oversee and provide expert technical direction for technology-based processes. This individual's principal goals are to develop and manage specific technical environments for each department and to attain all IT service level agreements for the user community within the organization. The lead will plan and provide direction and support for IT solutions that enhance mission-critical business operations. This position will work closely with decision makers in other departments to identify, recommend, develop, implement, and support cost-effective solutions for all aspects of the organization. This person will also help to define and implement IT policies, standards, procedures, and best practices. Responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to the following: provide technical direction and recommendations to team members and IS management; understand and ensure compliance to IS standards and methodology; recommend and develop plans for systems development and operations; hardware, software and equipment purchases; negotiate with technical personnel and customers for services, products and direction; review and advise groups in the selection, usage and maintenance of technology solutions; provide direction to the vendors and stay current on the latest technologies of the systems supported by the organization to assist in the future planning of necessary IT initiatives; other duties as assigned.

REQUIREMENTS
Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or other technical area. Equivalent work experience may be acceptable.

Experience: 6+ years of experience in Information Systems or related area with proven programming experience.

Computer Skills: Strong knowledge of multiple technologies including but not limited to SCADA, 4GL programming, scripting, server based, and SQL.

PLC Skills: Knowledge in programming, commissioning, and troubleshooting PLC-based control systems in industrial environments. Experienced with ladder logic and structured programming, I/O mapping, HMI integration, and interpreting electrical schematics to diagnose faults and restore uptime.

Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Experience communicating technical information to non-technical team members

Special Skills: Advanced understanding and experience with a System Development Lifecycle Methodology; advanced experience developing, reviewing, and/or modifying specifications, configurations, and programs to meet specified requirements; experience in the following: analyzing and interpreting information systems proposals, evaluating and developing alternative implementation plans, reviewing and developing coding standards and working productively in a cross functional team advanced knowledge of relevant multi-user computer systems, applications, and/or equipment; knowledge of current technology developments and trends; extensive problem-solving skills; experience developing and executing integrated test plans; basic project management capabilities.

• PLC / Controls: Strong hands-on PLC troubleshooting and programming experience, with Schneider Electric / Modicon being particularly important. They should be comfortable working in an environment containing both newer and legacy controls.
• Plant Automation: Troubleshooting automated production and material-handling equipment in a live manufacturing environment.
• Conveyance / Material Handling: Controls experience supporting conveyors, motors/drives, sensors, photo eyes, interlocks, sequencing, and related material-handling equipment.
• Scanning / Identification Systems: Experience integrating and troubleshooting industrial barcode/scanning/vision equipment. Our environment includes Keyence, Cognex and SICK, so experience with those platforms would be highly relevant.
• SCADA / HMI (Ignition and iFix): Ability to diagnose issues across PLC, HMI/SCADA and connected equipment rather than treating the PLC as an isolated system.
• Industrial Networks / Communications: Ability to troubleshoot communications between PLCs, scanners, field devices, HMIs and other plant-floor systems.
• Upgrades & Modernization: Comfortable supporting older equipment while also helping with controls upgrades, replacements and modernization efforts.
• Plant-Floor Troubleshooting: Strong diagnostic ability—someone who can trace a problem across controls, electrical, communications and equipment to determine the actual root cause rather than simply replacing components.

Travel: This position is for onsite presence for Holcomb, KS plant.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Semiconductor Equipment Maintenance Technician

Location: Albuquerque, NM
Shift: 6am -6pm (Sun-Tues AND Sun - Wed -- every other week)
Pay: $35-$45 hourly +Monthly KPI based Bonus 

****Direct hire - NOT contract or temp

Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced Semiconductor Equipment Maintenance Technician to support the maintenance, troubleshooting, calibration, and continuous improvement of semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment. This position will work in a cleanroom manufacturing environment supporting advanced production equipment and thin-film semiconductor processes.
The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience maintaining semiconductor processing equipment, strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills, and the ability to safely work with complex vacuum, chemical, and process systems.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Maintain standard operating conditions on assigned semiconductor production and facility-related equipment.
  • Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment and supporting systems.
  • Perform preventative maintenance, equipment inspections, alignments, and calibrations in accordance with manufacturer and internal specifications.
  • Support thin-film semiconductor production equipment, including:
    • LPV – Low Pressure Vapor processes/equipment
    • LPCVD – Low Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition
    • CVD – Chemical Vapor Deposition
    • PVD – Physical Vapor Deposition
  • Maintain and troubleshoot AMAT Epi reactors and ASM Epi reactors.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot Wet Benches and associated semiconductor processing systems.
  • Troubleshoot equipment and process issues involving mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, vacuum, temperature, and process-control systems.
  • Assist with equipment installation, setup, qualification, and process improvements.
  • Support semiconductor production equipment such as thin-film deposition systems, wafer fabrication equipment, wet benches, and related process equipment.
  • Assist in identifying root causes of equipment failures and implementing corrective actions.
  • Maintain and improve equipment and process Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Document preventative maintenance, repairs, calibrations, and equipment performance.
  • Assist with training employees on equipment operation, maintenance procedures, and safety requirements.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area in accordance with cleanroom and semiconductor manufacturing standards.
  • Follow all environmental, health, and safety (EHS) requirements, including proper PPE and chemical-handling procedures.
  • Participate in safety activities, drills, meetings, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Perform other maintenance and technical duties as assigned.
Required Qualifications
  • Associate degree, technical degree, certificate, or equivalent combination of education and hands-on experience.
  • 2+ years of experience working with semiconductor wafer fabrication or semiconductor manufacturing equipment preferred.
  • Experience troubleshooting and maintaining complex production equipment.
  • Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes and cleanroom protocols.
  • Experience with LPV, LPCVD, CVD, and/or PVD thin-film equipment strongly preferred.
  • Ability to troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, vacuum, and process-control systems.
  • Ability to safely work with chemicals and follow established EHS procedures.
  • Strong understanding of preventative maintenance, equipment calibration, and troubleshooting techniques.
  • Ability to read and follow technical documentation, equipment specifications, and SOPs.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to work effectively in a highly controlled manufacturing environment.
Preferred Semiconductor Equipment Experience

Experience with one or more of the following is highly desirable:
  • LPV equipment
  • LPCVD systems
  • CVD systems
  • PVD systems
  • Thin-film deposition equipment
  • Semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment
  • Vacuum systems
  • Wet benches
  • Gas delivery systems
  • Process control systems
  • Temperature control systems
  • Semiconductor cleanroom equipment
  • Equipment alignment and calibration

Work Environment
This is an on-site semiconductor manufacturing position requiring work in a cleanroom/controlled manufacturing environment. The technician must be comfortable working around complex equipment, chemicals, vacuum systems, and semiconductor production processes while following strict safety and contamination-control procedures.

CTD113

job.title: Production Associate - 1st Shift
job.description:
Are you ready to kick-start your career journey with Nesco Resource at Altec Industries in Elizabethtown? We're on the lookout for driven individuals who crave more than just a job – those who seek a production position within an innovative work environment brimming with opportunities for professional growth and advancement. At Altec, your work isn't just a task; it's impactful, valued, and prioritized above all else – including safety. While we require strong attendance and initiative, rest assured, their unmatched training program will equip you for success every step of the way.

This position is Monday through Friday, first shift hours 7am - 3:30pm with a 30 minute lunch break.
Must have third shift availability.


PURPOSE OF POSITION:
To install parts and components on trucks according to company and customer specifications.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Read work orders to determine customer requirements. Provide quality and timely workmanship on each work order.
  • Read schematics to install various components such as hydraulic valves, pumps, oil tanks, flow regulators, pressure switches, etc.
  • Read drawings and use tape measure.
  • Using impact tools, install outriggers, huck bolts, sub frames, and mechanical/hydraulic winches, and any associated equipment per the customer's request.
  • Install ladder racks, steps and grab handles to truck body.
  • Use small and large manual hand tools to bolt assembly components to truck chassis.
  • Drill holes and mount all specified electrical apparatus.
  • Install fuse panel for all electrical accessories.
  • Tape/cover parts of truck not to be painted.
  • Perform touch-up paint procedures as needed.
  • Perform quality and safety checks according to company and customer specifications.

Employment Type: Full-Time

Position Summary

The Production Operator is responsible for safely operating manual and automated machinery to manufacture, assemble, package, and label high-quality products in a cleanroom environment. This role is responsible for following established work instructions, SOPs, GMPs, and quality standards to ensure products are manufactured accurately, safely, and on schedule.

The ideal candidate is dependable, detail-oriented, quality-focused, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, regulated manufacturing environment.

Essential Responsibilities

This position operates in both manufacturing and office environments. The employee will regularly work around manufacturing machinery, production equipment, and company products.

job.title: HR Recruiter
job.description:
Talent Acquisition Recruiter – Manufacturing

Employment Type: Contract (Approximately 6 Months)
Schedule: Monday – Friday, 7:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Primary Focus: High-Volume Manufacturing & Hourly Recruiting
Reporting Structure: Works under the day-to-day guidance of the Talent Acquisition Team Leader

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Talent Acquisition Recruiter to support a significant increase in hiring needs over the next six months.

This position will be responsible for managing full-cycle recruiting activities, with a primary focus on hourly manufacturing positions, including assemblers, machinists, stockroom associates, shipping personnel, and quality inspectors.

The ideal candidate will have experience recruiting in a manufacturing environment, managing multiple open requisitions, coordinating interviews, facilitating offers, and supporting pre-employment screening and onboarding activities.

This role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to build effective relationships with hiring managers and HR leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Full-Cycle Recruiting & Talent Acquisition

  • Manage full-cycle recruiting activities for hourly manufacturing positions.

  • Create and manage job requisitions using the company's internal recruiting system.

job.title: Production Technician I - 1st Shift
job.description:
Production Operator – Dyneema Manufacturing

Location: Mesa, AZ
Schedule: Monday–Thursday (4 Days per Week)
Shift: 1st Shift | 4:00 AM – 2:30 PM

Position Summary

We are seeking a dependable, safety-conscious, and detail-oriented Production Operator to support Dyneema manufacturing operations in Mesa, AZ.

This position is responsible for setting up, operating, monitoring, adjusting, and maintaining production equipment to manufacture high-quality products according to established specifications, work instructions, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

The ideal candidate has previous manufacturing experience, strong mechanical aptitude, and the ability to troubleshoot equipment, maintain accurate production records, and work safely in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Candidates must have at least one year of manufacturing experience or equivalent military technical experience or training.

Essential Responsibilities

Manufacturing & Equipment Operation

  • Set up, operate, monitor, adjust, and clean manufacturing equipment according to established work instructions and SOPs.

  • Monitor production processes to ensure equipment operates safely and efficiently while meeting quality and production standards.

  • Perform equipment changeovers, machine setups, and routine cleaning procedures.

  • Adjust process settings within established limits to maintain product quality and specifications.

  • Read and interpret gauges, meters, dials, and equipment controls.

  • Identify equipment malfunctions and perform basic troubleshooting to minimize production downtime.

  • Complete minor preventive maintenance and routine equipment inspections.

  • Operate assigned production equipment and maintain proficiency in required manufacturing processes.

Quality Control & Production Documentation

  • Perform in-process quality inspections to ensure products meet established standards.

  • Collect and prepare samples of intermediate and finished products for quality testing.

  • Identify product defects, process irregularities, and potential quality concerns.

  • Maintain accurate production records, work orders, and equipment logs.

  • Enter raw material, component, and finished product information into computerized tracking systems.

  • Follow established production recipes, specifications, and quality requirements.

  • Communicate equipment, material, and product quality concerns to the team lead or supervisor.

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives to improve product quality, productivity, and manufacturing efficiency.

Material Handling & Inventory

  • Move raw materials, intermediate products, and finished goods throughout the manufacturing facility.

  • Operate material-handling equipment, including pallet jacks, forklifts, and overhead cranes.

  • Maintain appropriate inventory levels of raw materials, components, and production supplies.

  • Ensure materials are properly handled, stored, and tracked according to company procedures.

  • Perform manual material handling and heavy lifting as required.

Safety, Compliance & Housekeeping

  • Follow all Safety, Health, Environment (SHE), security, and company operating procedures.

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe manufacturing environment.

  • Identify and report unsafe conditions, near misses, incidents, and potential hazards.

  • Follow applicable regulatory requirements, safety procedures, and manufacturing standards.

  • Handle hazardous materials and waste according to established safety and environmental procedures, when assigned.

  • Maintain required hazardous waste documentation and support inspections or emergency response activities as applicable.

  • Participate in safety investigations, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and Job Safety Analysis (JSA) activities.

  • Follow company confidentiality, security, and intellectual property protection policies.

  • Participate in safety, quality, and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Complete required training and maintain current training records.

  • Perform additional manufacturing duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Minimum of 1 year of manufacturing experience, or equivalent military technical experience or training.

  • Experience operating, setting up, cleaning, or maintaining manufacturing equipment.

  • Ability to follow detailed work instructions, SOPs, and production specifications.

  • Basic mechanical aptitude and equipment troubleshooting skills.

  • Knowledge of manufacturing safety procedures and quality requirements.

  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Word and Access.

  • Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations.

  • Ability to read gauges, meters, dials, and equipment controls.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify product defects or equipment issues.

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills in English.

  • Ability to maintain accurate production records and documentation.

Preferred:

  • Previous experience in textile, composites, or similar manufacturing environments.

  • Experience with manufacturing equipment changeovers and preventive maintenance.

  • Experience operating forklifts, pallet jacks, or overhead cranes.

  • Experience handling hazardous materials or working in safety-regulated manufacturing environments.

  • Familiarity with computerized production tracking and inventory systems.

Position: Automation Equipment Mechanic
Location: Scottsville, NY

Summary: Nesco Resource is seeking an experienced Automation Equipment Mechanic to support precision medical device manufacturing operations in Scottsville, NY. This direct hire role serves as a key technical resource for troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining complex automated manufacturing equipment, including injection molding machinery and downstream automation systems.

The Automation Equipment Mechanic will diagnose electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and process-related issues, perform preventative maintenance, and support equipment improvements to minimize downtime and maintain production efficiency. This position also serves as a primary escalation point for equipment troubleshooting, providing technical guidance and training to maintenance mechanics and production operators.

The ideal candidate will have a strong electro-mechanical background, experience troubleshooting automated manufacturing equipment, and the ability to work with PLC-controlled systems in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

Pay Rate:

  • $30.00 - $41.00/Hour, Based On Experience
    • + 15% Night Shift Differential

Shift(s):

  • 6:00 PM - 6:00 AM, Rotating Night Schedule
    • Week 1: Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday
    • Week 2: Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday
      • Mandatory overtime may be required based on production and business needs

  • Troubleshoot, diagnose, repair, and maintain complex automated manufacturing equipment, including injection molding machines and downstream automation cells
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for troubleshooting automated manufacturing equipment failures
  • Diagnose and resolve electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and process-related issues affecting manufacturing equipment

Requirements:

  • Minimum of 3 years of maintenance experience in controls, electro-mechanical maintenance, or a related technical field

  • Completion of an apprenticeship, military technical training program, or trade school with relevant experience preferred
  • Strong understanding of electrical and mechanical systems
  • Experience troubleshooting and repairing automated manufacturing equipment
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, blueprints, and technical documentation
  • Strong troubleshooting, diagnostic, and problem-solving skills

  • Good verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical information clearly

  • CNC equipment experience
  • Injection molding machine experience

  • Machine shop experience, including lathe and mill operation
  • Experience supporting automated manufacturing cells and precision equipment
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications

Physical Requirements:

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Recruiter to manage full-cycle recruiting across a growing industrial operation. This role supports hiring for production, skilled trades, engineering, technical, professional, and leadership positions while partnering closely with hiring managers to meet workforce needs.

The ideal candidate has a strong background in manufacturing or industrial recruiting, can manage multiple openings simultaneously, and knows how to build talent pipelines for both high-volume and hard-to-fill positions. Bilingual English/Spanish skills are preferred to help support a diverse workforce.

Key Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition

  • Maintain a positive candidate experience throughout the hiring process

Sourcing Strategy

  • Utilize job boards, social media, networking, referrals, staffing partners, and recruiting events to identify talent

job.title: Tool Maker
job.description:
Tool Maker in Hauppauge, NY:
Direct Hire
Salary Range: $120- 170,000

We are seeking a hands-on, detail-oriented Tool Maker with strong experience in metalworking, CNC and precision machining to support new and existing products from concept through production.
This role requires deep technical knowledge of turn/mill machining centers, grinding to tight tolerances, and CAD/CAM tools such as SolidWorks and SolidCam. The ideal candidate will bring a strong design and innovation mindset, creating and refining designs for new and existing metal or CNC-machined products, lead cross-functional projects, improve product designs for manufacturability, develop robust manufacturing methods, and work closely with suppliers to source high-quality components and services.
This is a great opportunity to join One of Long Island's most secure and diverse manufacturers servicing a wide variety of markets with excellent growth opportunity.

Key Responsibilities of the Tool Maker in Hauppauge, NY:
Create innovative designs for new metal and CNC-machined products, and continuously refine and improve existing product designs for performance, manufacturability, and cost.
Develop, document, and optimize manufacturing processes for precision metal components and assemblies.
Provide technical expertise in turn/mill machining centers, grinding operations, tooling, fixturing, and precision inspection methods.
Create and maintain manufacturing methods, routings, work instructions, setup documentation, and process controls to support efficient, repeatable production.
Lead projects from concept through implementation, coordinating activities across engineering, production, quality, and supply chain teams.
Design and redesign products, tooling, and processes with a strong focus on ease of manufacturing, cost effectiveness, quality, and scalability.
Use SolidWorks to support product and fixture design, and SolidCam to develop machining strategies and improve CNC programming efficiency.
Drive design innovation by exploring new materials, geometries, and machining approaches that improve product performance while reducing production complexity and cost.
Analyze production challenges, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve throughput, yield, and product quality.
Support grinding and machining operations that require tight tolerances, fine surface finishes, and consistent process capability.
Collaborate with production teams to improve workflow, reduce setup time, and standardize best practices.
Source components, raw materials, tooling, and outside services from qualified suppliers; evaluate supplier capabilities, quality, cost, and lead time.
Work with vendors and suppliers to support prototype development, new part introduction, cost reduction, and ongoing supply continuity.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to safety, quality, delivery, and manufacturing efficiency.

Qualifications of the Tool Maker in Hauppauge, NY:
Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
5+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in a metalworking or precision machining environment.
Strong knowledge of turn/mill machining centers, CNC machining practices, grinding processes, and tolerance-critical manufacturing.
Proven ability to design and innovate new metal or CNC-machined products, translating concepts into manufacturable, cost-effective designs.
Proficiency in SolidWorks and SolidCam or similar platforms,
Demonstrated ability to lead projects and guide cross-functional teams through implementation and process improvement efforts.
Experience with design for manufacturability (DFM), process development, and new product introduction.
Experience developing comprehensive manufacturing methods and process documentation.
Excellent problem-solving, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively with diverse teams and individuals across all levels of the organization
 

A comprehensive benefits package will be offered which includes Medical, Vision, Dental, 401K, and paid time off.

job.title: Logistics Specialist
job.description:
100% fully onsite; M-F, 8am-5pm

Summary
The Logistics Specialist supports end-to-end product flow across hazardous materials, R&D materials, clinical drug product distribution, and inventory management operations. This role ensures compliant, accurate, and timely execution of shipping, receiving, inventory control, and documentation activities while adhering to internal SOPs, regulatory standards, and quality expectations. This position is designated as 100% onsite due to the essential nature of the job functions.

Responsibilities:
Process hazardous materials, R&D materials, and product sample shipments. Manage international shipments, including documentation and proper packaging.
Receive and dispense finished goods, WIP inventory, and packaging components to and from manufacturing facilities.
Pick, pack, and ship clinical finished drug products to domestic and international destinations.
Process rejected, returned, or expired drug products for destruction.
Coordinate and schedule destruction activities with approved destruction sites.
Maintain the inventory control system for drug products.
Conduct inventory cycle counts and ensure accurate reconciliation results.
Maintain equipment and work areas in a clean, safe, and compliant manner. Safely operate material-handling equipment.
Become fully proficient in applicable SOPs and perform responsibilities with minimal supervision. Recommend changes or updates to SOPs as needed. Participate in the training of new team members.
Access internal systems, databases, and RF scanners; ensure accurate data entry and documentation. File and store documentation according to corporate retention policies.

Requirements
High school diploma with 0–5 years of relevant experience.
Knowledge of warehouse operations, inventory systems, and inventory control concepts.
IATA certification and international shipping documentation experience (preferred).
Ability to meet TSA requirements, including successful background check. Ability to complete the Certified Cargo Screening Program (CCSP).
Experience with warehouse material-handling equipment (preferred).
Strong attention to detail and prioritization skills. Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively in a cooperative team environment. Ability to work occasional overtime.
Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

job.title: Material Handler
job.description:
Title: Material Handler
Location: Cleveland, OH 44135
Pay: $18.00 to $20.00
Schedule: 12-hour rotating shifts, Days and Nights are available!

Keep Production Moving!

Are you dependable, hands-on, and comfortable working in a fast-paced warehouse and manufacturing environment? Do you enjoy staying active and take pride in keeping things organized and moving in the right direction?

Nesco Resource is hiring Material Handlers for US Cotton in Cleveland!

As a Material Handler, you'll play an important role in keeping production running smoothly. You'll move finished products, deliver raw materials and supplies to production areas, load trucks, help maintain inventory, and make sure materials get where they need to be when they need to be there.

This is a hands-on position that combines forklift operation, warehouse work, inventory tracking, and material movement. If you like staying busy and being an important part of a production team, this could be a great opportunity for you.

What You'll Do:

• Operate a forklift to move materials and finished products throughout the warehouse and production areas.
• Retrieve daily work orders and gather the materials needed for production.
• Review daily checklists and make sure required materials are available.
• Transport raw materials from the warehouse to the appropriate production areas.
• Load materials onto pallets by hand or with a forklift, including materials weighing up to 35 lbs.
• Move finished pallets out of receiving areas using a pallet jack.
• Enter material information into the company's computer/database system.
• Scan finished products and prepare shipments for loading.
• Load finished products onto trucks using a forklift.
• Manually enter product and shipment information into the computer system.
• Inspect trucks for damage and report any issues before loading.
• Check industrial truck wheels and locks as part of routine loading procedures.
• Enter bills of lading into the computer for shipments.
• Wrap finished-product pallets with plastic wrap and prepare them for shipment.
• Use an order picker and ladder when retrieving products from designated storage areas.
• Maintain an organized and clean warehouse and work area.
• Use an air hose, broom, dustpan, and other cleaning equipment to remove debris and production remnants.
• Communicate with maintenance when equipment or wrapping equipment requires attention.
• Assist with forklift battery changes and other warehouse tasks as needed.
• Follow all required safety procedures and wear appropriate PPE.

The ideal candidate will:

• Be comfortable operating or learning to operate a forklift.
• Be able to work safely around moving equipment, forklifts, production areas, and warehouse traffic.
• Have good attention to detail when handling materials and preparing shipments.
• Be comfortable using a computer, keyboard, scanner, and other basic warehouse technology.
• Be able to follow work orders, checklists, and established procedures.
• Be comfortable lifting boxes and materials weighing up to approximately 35 lbs.
• Be comfortable frequently getting on and off a forklift.
• Be able to bend, reach, push, pull, and move materials throughout the workday.
• Be dependable and able to work as part of a team.
• Be willing to maintain a clean and organized work area.
• Have a strong commitment to workplace safety.

job.title: Accounting Specialist
job.description:
Accounting Specialist – Accounts Payable (AP)

Location: Iron Mountain, MI
Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite
Schedule: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM
Employment Type: Contract
Contract Duration: Through February 2027

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented Accounting Specialist – Accounts Payable (AP) to support daily accounts payable operations, invoice processing, vendor reconciliation, and financial recordkeeping.

Working under the direction of Accounting Coordinators, this position will be responsible for processing supplier invoices, resolving discrepancies, maintaining accurate accounting records, and ensuring timely payments.

The Accounting Specialist may also assist with month-end closing activities, project costing, audits, and special accounting projects. This role requires frequent communication with suppliers, employees, and internal business partners to resolve issues and ensure accurate financial transactions.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable & Invoice Processing

  • Process supplier invoices for payment using the company's ERP system, SyteLine.

  • Review and match supplier invoices with receiving documentation and purchase orders.

  • Perform three-way matching of invoices, purchase orders, and receiving records.

  • Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies related to purchase orders, receiving documentation, or payment amounts.

  • Obtain appropriate approvals for service invoices and non-purchase-order payments.

  • Assign accurate general ledger account codes to non-PO invoices.

  • Voucher invoices for payment in accordance with established accounting procedures.

  • Support weekly accounts payable processing activities.

  • Ensure timely and accurate recording of accounts payable transactions.

Vendor Reconciliation & Communication

  • Verify and reconcile vendor statements to ensure accuracy.

  • Respond to vendor inquiries regarding invoices, payments, and account discrepancies.

  • Research and resolve outstanding payment issues.

  • Collaborate with Purchasing, Receiving, and other internal departments to resolve accounts payable matters.

  • Escalate unresolved issues appropriately and provide timely follow-up.

  • Maintain professional relationships with vendors, employees, and internal business partners.

Accounting Support & Recordkeeping

  • Maintain accurate electronic filing systems for invoices and supporting documentation.

  • Ensure financial records are complete, organized, and accessible.

  • Assist with month-end closing activities as needed.

  • Support project costing and other accounting-related functions.

  • Assist with internal and external audits by gathering documentation and reconciling information.

  • Participate in special accounting projects and process improvement initiatives.

  • Perform additional accounting and administrative duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

  • Associate degree in Accounting or a related field preferred.

  • Minimum of 2 years of office or administrative experience required.

  • At least 1 year of accounting or accounts payable experience preferred.

  • Previous experience processing invoices, reconciling vendor accounts, or supporting accounts payable functions is desirable.

  • Experience working with ERP or accounting software preferred.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Outlook.

  • Experience working with ERP or accounting software.

  • Familiarity with accounts payable processes, invoice processing, and vendor reconciliation.

  • Understanding of purchase orders, invoice matching, and accounting documentation.

  • Strong data entry skills with a high degree of accuracy.

  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to research and resolve discrepancies efficiently.

  • Strong time management skills and ability to meet deadlines.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.

  • Comfortable communicating with vendors, employees, and cross-functional departments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using Infor SyteLine ERP.

  • Previous accounts payable or accounting support experience.

  • Experience with three-way invoice matching.

  • Familiarity with purchase order processing and non-PO invoice approvals.

  • Experience with vendor statement reconciliations.

  • Exposure to month-end close, general ledger coding, or accounting audits.

  • Experience working in a manufacturing or industrial environment.

job.title: Glue Adjuster
job.description:
Glue Machine Adjuster
Location: Roanoke, VA
Direct Hire opportunity 
 

Are you an experienced gluer operator ready to take the next step in your career? This is a working lead opportunity with direct crew responsibility — a clear path toward a supervisory role for someone who combines hands-on technical skill with the ability to train, coach, and drive results on the floor. If you've got years in folding carton or sheet-fed lithography and you're ready to own a shift, this is worth a look.

 

Produces high-quality printed material to job specifications by setting up and operating gluing equipment and related auxiliaries. Responsible for achieving and maintaining adhesion quality to customer standards, coordinating and developing machine crew, documenting production results, and keeping equipment and supplies in order.

 
Responsibilities:

  • Execute the daily shift production schedule
  • Coordinate, train, and develop the glue machine crew; assign responsibilities and enforce safe work practices, housekeeping, GMP, and quality procedures
  • Document shift performance and report production results
  • Read and interpret job orders and specifications
  • Determine materials needed to fulfill order requirements
  • Organize job sequence on machine; ensure next job is staged and ready for make-ready
  • Retrieve required glue materials and WIP as needed
  • Perform machine make-ready using available make-ready stock
  • Achieve and maintain glue and adhesion quality in line with process and quality specifications
  • Inspect finished product to verify quality and process control; take corrective action on deviations
  • Troubleshoot machine stoppages and downtime; conduct periodic maintenance checks and assist maintenance personnel with repairs as needed
  • Maintain clean and organized work area
  • Return excess consumables and materials to designated storage locations
  • Follow all safety rules and regulations
  • Additional duties as assigned by finishing leadership
 
Skills & Abilities:
  • Able to read, write, record, and communicate production data effectively
  • Strong time management and follow-through
  • Solid troubleshooting and problem analysis skills
  • Demonstrated ability to build, coach, and develop a crew
  • Computer literate
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Good color vision
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required
  • 5 years of experience in a sheet-fed lithography or folding carton operation
  • 3 years of progressive manufacturing experience
  • Demonstrated track record of improvement in quality and efficiency
  • Previous experience with Pallet jack; folder-gluer equipment including Bobst, Alpina, Jagenberg, and International platforms
  • Ability to pass a preemployment screening

 
Salary $20-$25 an hour based on experience
Shift 2nd (Monday through Friday 2 pm to 10 pm)

RELOCATION BONUS AVAILABLE

job.title: CNC Mill Machinist
job.description:
CNC Mill Machinist Phoenix, AZ · On-site · Full-time

Join a leading aerospace manufacturer in Phoenix where precision matters and your skills drive mission-critical components. We're hiring experienced CNC machinists who can set up, run, and prove out parts on modern Fanuc-controlled mills and lathes— multiple shifts available.

Pay Range: $25–$35/hr
Shifts: 2nd (M–Th)(+8% Shift Differential)

What You'll Do

  • Set up and operate CNC vertical/horizontal mills and/or lathes (Fanuc controls)
  • Perform full setups, changeovers, and prove-outs on 3-, 4-, and 5-axis jobs
  • Use machine probing (Renishaw preferred) for work offsets and in-cycle verification
  • Read complex blueprints with strong GD&T comprehension (datum structures, true position, profile)
  • Hold tight tolerances (±0.001 " or better) on aerospace-grade parts
  • Troubleshoot issues (vibration, tool wear, tolerance drift) and maintain quality

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of CNC mill and/or lathe experience in aerospace or tight-tolerance manufacturing
  • Proven ability to perform independent setups and program prove-outs
  • Strong Fanuc controls experience
  • Solid GD&T knowledge (datum structures, true position, profile, etc.)
  • Familiarity with machine probing (Renishaw preferred)
  • Reliable, safety-minded, and detail-oriented

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technician
Location: Ravenna, OH
 
Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Maintenance Technician to support the safe and efficient operation of manufacturing equipment. This position will troubleshoot, maintain, and repair electrical, electronic, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mixing, and extrusion equipment. The ideal candidate has strong troubleshooting skills, a solid manufacturing maintenance background, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.
 
Job duties to include but not limited to:

  • Troubleshoot, maintain, and repair electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mixing, and extrusion equipment.
  • Read and interpret electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and automation drawings.
  • Perform mechanical repairs on conveyors, pumps, valves, motors, and mechanical drives.
  • Complete and document preventive maintenance and TPM activities.
  • Perform basic electrical repairs, welding/fabrication, and HVAC troubleshooting as needed.
  • Follow all safety procedures, including lockout/tagout and permit-to-work requirements.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Provide after-hours/weekend maintenance support and work overtime as needed.
  • Support equipment installations, modifications, and critical spare-parts planning.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Additional experience in the following areas is a plus:
  • HVAC troubleshooting
  • Welding and fabrication
  • Construction-related work, including concrete, masonry, electrical, HVAC, and plumbing
Qualifications & Skills
  • 1–3 years of maintenance experience in a manufacturing environment required; 5+ years preferred.
  • Strong working knowledge of electrical/electronic, hydraulic, mechanical, and pneumatic systems.
  • Experience coordinating or managing outside service providers for specialized equipment installation, maintenance, and repairs.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and daily maintenance activities while meeting deadlines.
  • Ability to work effectively with supervisors and cross-functional teams to identify problems and determine solutions.
  • Working knowledge of rotating equipment such as blowers, station equipment such as hoppers, and electric equipment such as motors.
  • Familiarity with OSHA, NFPA, EPA, and other applicable regulations.
  • Comfortable using workplace technology, including scheduling, inventory, and related software.
  • Ability to operate a tow motor and pallet jack.
  • Comfortable working in a variety of environments, including interior/exterior areas, confined spaces, elevated platforms, and heights.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
 
Salary $27-$38 an hour based on experinence
Hours of 3rd shift: Sunday evening to Friday morning - 10:45 PM to 7:15 AM
3rd Shift Premium: $1.50 per hour
 
There may be scheduled overtime on Saturday depending on business need.

job.title: Chemical Technician
job.description:
Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Assist with chemical processing operations under the direction of Chem Tech II, Chem Tech III, Process Technologist, and/or Management.
  • Load, wash, rack, and move parts as directed.
  • Perform visual inspections of parts before, during, and after processing to ensure adherence to specifications and quality standards.
  • Verify chemical bath concentrations and report any deviations promptly.
  • Monitor processing equipment and promptly report irregularities, malfunctions, or safety concerns.
  • Maintain cleanliness and organization of the work area and comply with all safety and environmental procedures.

 

Requirement Skills/Abilities:

  • Multi-stage cleaning processes: ultrasonic cleaning, DI water rinsing, acid passivation, and final drying.
  • Use of cleanroom-compatible chemicals, equipment, and procedures.
  • Final packaging performed in cleanroom conditions using UHV-compatible bags.

job.title: Manufacturing Engineer
job.description:
Manufacturing Engineer
Location: Avon, OH

We are seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to optimize production processes, support new product launches, and drive continuous improvement in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for developing manufacturing methods, implementing new equipment and automation, improving quality and productivity through Lean initiatives, and collaborating with engineering, production, maintenance, and customers to deliver efficient, cost-effective manufacturing solutions. The ideal candidate has a strong background in manufacturing engineering, CAD design, ERP systems, and process improvement, with experience supporting custom manufacturing and capital equipment projects.

Job duties

  • Develop, document, and improve manufacturing processes, methods, tooling, and work instructions to meet product specifications and ISO 9001:2015 standards.
  • Convert engineering designs into manufacturing documentation, including ERP routings, SolidWorks drawings, fixtures, and setup procedures.
  • Lead new product launches, prototype builds, first-article inspections, and capital equipment projects from design through commissioning and operator training.
  • Design and implement automated and semi-automated equipment, tooling, fixtures, and safe workstations in collaboration with Maintenance.
  • Drive Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives using production metrics, SQDC, root cause analysis, and waste reduction techniques.
  • Analyze production data to improve safety, quality, productivity, and overall manufacturing performance.
  • Provide technical support, cost estimates, project proposals, and customer-focused manufacturing solutions.
  • Support OSHA safety initiatives and maintain compliance with ISO 9001:2015 quality systems, audits, and corrective actions.

Requirements
  • Bachelor of Science in Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and hands-on manufacturing experience.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years' experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of SolidWorks and AutoCAD, 2D and 3D design.
  • ERP system proficiency (routings, BOMs); Syteline or SAP preferred.
  • Experience handling customer proposals, quotes, and pricing.
  • Ability to interact effectively with customers, management, and inter- and intra-departmental co-workers, including sales and production personnel. Heavy interaction and consultation with Production Supervisors.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, along with exceptional interpersonal and organizational skills.
  • Experience in copper or nonferrous metals fabrication, high-current electrical products, or custom/engineer-to-order job-shop manufacturing.
  • Hands-on knowledge of CNC machining, waterjet or laser cutting, and welding/brazing/press-welding processes.
  • Lean manufacturing training or certification (e.g., Six Sigma Green Belt); experience leading Kaizen, 5S, or value stream mapping events.

Candidates MUST have hands-on semiconductor equipment maintenance and troubleshooting experience. Experience maintaining thin-film, deposition, epitaxial, or semiconductor processing equipment is required.

Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite – 5 Days per Week

Experience Required: Entry-Level (0–1 Years)

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented and dependable Lockbox Operations Specialist to support high-volume banking and payment processing operations.

This position focuses on opening and sorting incoming mail, extracting checks and payment documents, organizing and batching transactions, and performing accurate data entry in a fast-paced, production-driven environment.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong attention to detail, accurate 10-key data entry skills, reliability, and the ability to meet daily production goals while following established procedures.

This is a seasonal, fully onsite opportunity requiring consistent attendance, productivity, and the ability to work effectively within a team.

Key Responsibilities

Mail Processing & Document Extraction

  • Open incoming mail and extract paper invoices, checks, and payment documents.

  • Accurately separate and sort payment and non-payment documents for processing.

  • Review documents to ensure proper handling and organization.

  • Prepare, organize, and batch documents for subsequent processing.

  • Perform high-volume data entry and 10-key processing with a high degree of speed and accuracy.

  • Enter, verify, and process transaction information according to established procedures.

  • Support monetary processing functions while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

  • Ensure transactions and documentation are properly recorded, filed, and organized.

  • Meet established daily production, quality, and processing goals.

    • Retail and small business banking

    • Credit card processing

    • Consumer and mortgage lending

    • Collections and recovery

    • Loan origination and auto finance

  • Escalate processing concerns or operational issues to management when necessary.

Cross-Training & Team Support

  • Participate in cross-training to support critical department functions, including:

    • Mail sorting

    • Document extraction

    • Data entry and keying

    • Reassociation

    • Transaction batching

  • Collaborate with team members to maintain workflow efficiency and meet production deadlines.

  • Adapt to changing workloads and departmental priorities.

  • Perform basic scheduled and non-scheduled maintenance functions as assigned.

  • Complete additional operational or administrative duties as needed.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • 0–1 years of experience in banking operations, mail processing, data entry, general office administration, or a related environment.

  • Entry-level candidates with strong attention to detail and data entry abilities are encouraged to apply.

  • Previous experience in a production-driven or high-volume processing environment is beneficial.

Required Skills & Competencies

  • Proficiency in 10-key data entry, with strong speed and accuracy.

  • Exceptional attention to detail when handling financial documents and transactions.

  • Ability to process high transaction volumes accurately and efficiently.

  • Strong organizational and time management skills.

  • Ability to follow detailed procedures and instructions consistently.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

  • Comfortable navigating multiple computer systems and applications.

  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines and production goals.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to identify discrepancies and escalate concerns appropriately.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and sound judgment.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.

  • Dependable, adaptable, and willing to learn new tasks and processes.

  • Strong commitment to accuracy, productivity, and consistent attendance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience in lockbox processing, payment processing, banking operations, or financial services.

  • Experience with mail sorting, check extraction, and document batching.

  • High-volume data entry or transaction processing experience.

  • Familiarity with banking policies, procedures, and applicable regulations.

  • Previous experience handling checks, invoices, payments, or other financial documents.

  • Experience working in a production-based environment with daily performance metrics.

  • College degree preferred but not required.

Interview & Skills Testing Requirements

Candidates must be available for an onsite interview and required skills assessments.

The interview process will include:

  • Onsite interview with the hiring team.

Candidates should be comfortable completing hands-on testing during the interview process.

job.description:
Network Deployment Technician / Engineer – Ubiquiti & UniFi Infrastructure

Position Type: Project-Based Contract
Schedule: Monday – Friday | 7:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Local Time)
Openings: 4 Technicians/Engineers

Nesco Resource is seeking four (4) experienced Network Deployment Technicians/Engineers to support an onsite network infrastructure deployment project. This engagement involves the installation, configuration support, testing, and turn-up of Ubiquiti/UniFi networking equipment, including switches, gateways, wireless access points, UPS systems, and related infrastructure.

Ideal candidates will have hands-on experience with enterprise network hardware installations, rack-mounted equipment, structured cabling, and network connectivity troubleshooting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Unbox, stage, install, and deploy new network infrastructure equipment.

  • Install and connect UPS systems, power backup equipment, and PDUs.

  • Rack and mount network switches, gateways, and associated hardware.

  • Install wireless access points and wireless range extenders.

  • Install optical transceiver modules and connect existing fiber infrastructure.

  • Connect equipment to designated power outlets and network connections.

  • Perform equipment testing, connectivity verification, and initial turn-up.

  • Troubleshoot hardware, power, and network connectivity issues as needed.

  • Coordinate with onsite personnel to ensure equipment is installed according to project specifications.

  • Maintain an organized work area and dispose of packaging and debris in designated onsite locations.

Equipment Deployment Scope

The project includes installation and deployment of the following equipment:

Power Infrastructure

  • 2 UniFi UPS units

  • 19 Ubiquiti Power Backup units

  • 19 Ubiquiti Power Cables

  • 2 Ubiquiti PDUs

Network Infrastructure

  • 2 Ubiquiti Enterprise Fortress Gateways

  • 2 Ubiquiti Aggregation Switches

  • 3 Ubiquiti Layer 3 Switches

  • 19 Ubiquiti Pro XG 24 PoE Switches

Wireless Infrastructure

  • 3 Ubiquiti U7 Pro Wireless Extenders

  • 56 UniFi E7 Wireless Access Points

Optical Components

  • 12 Ubiquiti 100G LR Optical Modules

  • 54 Ubiquiti 25Gbps Optical Modules

Mounting & Supporting Equipment

  • 20 Client 6U Wall-Mount Racks

  • 20 Puroma Wall-Mounted Key Lock Boxes

Required Qualifications

  • Previous experience with network equipment installation, deployment, or field engineering.

  • Hands-on experience installing switches, routers, gateways, UPS systems, and PDUs.

  • Familiarity with Ubiquiti/UniFi networking equipment strongly preferred.

  • Experience with rack mounting, network cabling, and fiber optic connections.

  • Understanding of basic network connectivity, Layer 2/Layer 3 switching, and hardware troubleshooting.

  • Ability to install and verify wireless access points.

  • Comfortable working independently and collaboratively in an onsite deployment environment.

  • Ability to follow installation procedures, technical documentation, and onsite safety requirements.

Additional Project Details

  • All work will be performed onsite during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM – 4:00 PM local time.

job.title: Doffer
job.description:
Schedule: Wednesday-Friday 7pm-7am and every other Saturday (12 hour shifts)
Pay: $17/hr
Position Summary

The Doffer works at the finishing end of a nonwoven fiber production line and supports the Lead Operator with safe, efficient production. The main responsibility is to remove completed rolls from the line, inspect them, and package and load them according to the customer order.
In plain terms: when a roll of fiber material is finished, the Doffer safely takes it off the wind-up end of the line, checks it for visible defects, packages and labels it, and prepares it for the next step based on the work order.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Read the production schedule, work order, and pick list to confirm the correct material, tube core, packaging, and customer requirements.
  • Remove completed rolls from the production line (the process known as doffing).
  • Visually inspect the fiber and finished rolls for quality concerns and notify the Lead Operator or Shift Manager of any problems.
  • Package, label, and load finished material exactly as required by the customer order.
  • Keep the correct tube cores, packaging materials, and other production supplies stocked and ready for use.
  • Assist with production-line setup and operation as directed by the Lead Operator, and learn the purpose of the basic mechanical and electrical components of the wind-up equipment.
  • Remove processed waste and scrap and place it in the designated area.
  • Follow all safety requirements, including lockout/tagout procedures, and report unresolved safety concerns to the Shift Manager.
  • Keep the production line and surrounding work area clean, organized, and safe.
  • Communicate clearly with the Lead Operator, Shift Manager, and other team members to help meet production goals.
  • Perform other production duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Ability to read, write, and follow work instructions, production schedules, pick lists, safety procedures, and diagrams.
  • Basic math skills, including the ability to read a tape measure and interpret process-control charts.
  • Basic computer skills to complete equipment setup entries and enter production information.
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions, use good judgment, and work with limited supervision.
  • Strong attention to detail, dependable attendance, and the ability to work effectively with others.

Physical Requirements

This is an active manufacturing position. The employee must be able to stand and walk for extended periods; use hands to handle materials; reach, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, and occasionally sit. The employee must regularly lift or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift or move up to 50 pounds. Close vision is required for inspection work.

Work Environment

Work is performed in a manufacturing environment with moderate noise, heat, vibration, fumes, airborne fibers or particles, and moving mechanical equipment. Employees must follow required safety procedures, wear required personal protective equipment, and work cooperatively with coworkers. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

job.title: HR Coordinator / HR Assistant
job.description:
We are seeking a detail-oriented and motivated HR Coordinator / HR Administrator to support the Human Resources team of a growing, innovative company in Houston. This is an immediate opportunity to gain hands-on experience across multiple areas of HR while working directly with the HR Manager and VP of HR.

The company currently has approximately 80–100 employees and operates in a fast-paced, startup environment. The ideal candidate is someone who enjoys wearing multiple hats, learns new systems quickly, and is comfortable taking ownership of administrative tasks while supporting a growing organization.

This position will focus heavily on HR data accuracy, payroll and benefits administration, employee onboarding and offboarding, and general HR operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage employee onboarding and offboarding processes within the company's HRIS system (UKG).

  • Enter, maintain, and update employee information, ensuring accuracy and data integrity.

  • Set up and verify employee pay information, benefit elections, and payroll deductions.

  • Assist the HR team and Finance/Accounting departments with payroll reviews, audits, and reconciliation.

  • Support employee benefits administration, including new hire enrollment, qualifying life events, and open enrollment.

  • Maintain employee personnel files, I-9 documentation, and other HR records in accordance with compliance requirements.

  • Respond to general employee HR questions related to payroll, benefits, policies, and onboarding, escalating complex matters to HR leadership.

  • Identify and help correct discrepancies in HRIS, payroll, and benefits records.

  • Assist with HR projects, process improvements, and initiatives as the company continues to grow and transition into its next phase of operations.

  • Provide day-to-day administrative support to the HR Manager and VP of HR.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

  • 1–2 years of HR administration, HR coordination, payroll, or benefits experience preferred. Recent graduates with relevant internship or professional experience are encouraged to apply.

  • Experience working with an HRIS system required; UKG experience is a strong plus but not required.

  • Basic understanding of payroll processes, employee benefits, onboarding, and HR documentation.

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when reviewing employee data, payroll information, and benefits deductions.

  • Comfortable using Microsoft Excel and other administrative systems.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to learn new software, processes, and responsibilities quickly.

  • Excellent communication skills and a professional approach to handling confidential employee information.

What We're Looking For

We are especially interested in someone who is adaptable, analytical, eager to learn, and comfortable working in a startup environment.

Unlike a traditional HR administrative position with narrowly defined responsibilities, this opportunity offers exposure to multiple areas of HR. Priorities can change quickly, so the successful candidate must be comfortable managing different responsibilities and learning as they go.

Candidates who have previously supported a small business, startup, or growing organization may be particularly well suited for this opportunity.

Why This Opportunity?

  • Work directly with experienced HR leadership.

  • Gain valuable hands-on experience with UKG, payroll, benefits, and HR operations.

  • Build a broad foundation across multiple HR functions.

  • Join a growing organization during an exciting phase of development.

  • Opportunity to contribute to meaningful HR projects and process improvements.

job.description:
Maintenance Mechanic

A well-established industrial manufacturing facility is hiring a Maintenance Technician/Mechanics to support production equipment, overhead crane systems, and facility operations. This is a highly hands-on role for a strong industrial maintenance tech who enjoys troubleshooting, repairing, and keeping heavy equipment running safely and reliably.

Pay & Benefits

  • Type: Contract-To-Hire with conversion following 90+ days with company (based on attendance and performance)

What You’ll Do

  • Equipment Troubleshooting & Repair: Diagnose and repair electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems on industrial production equipment and cranes.

  • Overhead Crane Support: Inspect, troubleshoot, and support crane systems and related components.

  • Preventive Maintenance: Perform scheduled PMs, inspections, and corrective actions.

  • Mechanical Systems: Hands-on experience with hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

job.title: Electrical Design Engineer – Industrial Equipment
job.description:
Electrical Design Engineer – Industrial Equipment

Eligible candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and must NOT require current or future sponsorship (including Student Visas).

Tulsa, OK | Full-Time | Direct Hire | On-Site

Eligible candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and must NOT require current or future sponsorship (including Student Visas).

Pay & Benefits

  • $120,000–$150,000, depending on experience

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance

  • 401(k) with Company Match

  • Paid Vacation, Personal Time & Holidays

  • Life & Disability Insurance

  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • Ongoing Training & Career Growth Opportunities

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Electrical Design Engineer to join an established and growing manufacturing organization in Tulsa. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on developing electrical designs for custom industrial equipment and integrated systems.

You’ll take ownership of assigned projects from initial requirements and electrical design through drawing release and manufacturing support. Working alongside Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Project Management, and other internal teams, you’ll help develop reliable, practical electrical solutions that meet technical specifications, safety standards, and production requirements.

This opportunity is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex design challenges, working with industrial electrical systems, and seeing projects move from engineering concepts to completed equipment.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and develop electrical systems, equipment layouts, and assemblies for industrial applications.

  • Create detailed electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, interconnection drawings, conductor schedules, and bills of material (BOMs).

  • Review project requirements and technical specifications to develop electrical solutions that meet performance, safety, and operational needs.

  • Perform engineering calculations and apply applicable electrical codes and industry standards.

  • Coordinate with Mechanical Engineering to integrate electrical components into complete equipment designs.

  • Manage assigned engineering projects from initial design through drawing release and production.

  • Partner with Project Management to track schedules, coordinate deliverables, and meet project deadlines.

  • Support engineering changes, drawing revisions, and technical documentation.

  • Work directly with Manufacturing to troubleshoot design issues and improve equipment assembly and production efficiency.

  • Participate in design reviews, testing, quality verification, and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Coordinate with internal teams, suppliers, and customers to clarify technical requirements and resolve engineering questions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

  • Professional experience in industrial electrical design, electrical equipment engineering, or electrical product development.

  • Proficiency with 2D CAD software and the ability to produce detailed electrical engineering drawings.

  • Ability to read, interpret, and develop electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical specifications.

  • Working knowledge of industrial electrical systems, components, and equipment integration.

  • Familiarity with applicable electrical codes, engineering standards, and safe design practices.

  • Ability to perform engineering calculations and troubleshoot technical design challenges.

  • Experience maintaining BOMs, engineering drawings, and related technical documentation.

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to handle multiple priorities.

  • Effective communication skills and the ability to collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and project teams.

Experience That Could Be Helpful

  • Industrial power distribution equipment, motor control systems, or custom electrical assemblies.

  • Experience with low- and medium-voltage electrical systems.

  • Working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC/NFPA 70) and applicable UL standards.

  • Experience with AutoCAD or comparable electrical drafting and design software.

  • Familiarity with 3D CAD tools and electromechanical equipment integration.

  • Custom equipment manufacturing or engineered-to-order environments.

  • Understanding of equipment assembly, manufacturing processes, and production testing.

  • Experience with ERP or MRP systems used to manage engineering and production information.

  • Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or Professional Engineer (PE) licensure.

Who This Could Be a Great Fit For

This is more than a drafting position. We’re looking for an electrical engineer who understands how to develop a complete, workable design—not just produce drawings.

If you enjoy translating technical requirements into electrical designs, solving equipment integration challenges, and collaborating with manufacturing to bring engineered systems to life, this role offers the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful projects from design through production.
