Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. Must have the ability to use microscope entire working day and sit for long periods with intermittent breaks to rest eyes and stretch. job.title: Business Operations Analyst
job.description:
Business Operations Analyst

Location Requirement: Candidates must be able to work onsite in Hauppauge, NY four days per week. Relocation assistance is not available.

 

Position Objective

The Business Analyst III, Sales Operations, supports a medical device sales organization by delivering data-driven insights, maintaining reporting infrastructure, and supporting accurate sales compensation and performance management. This role manages large, complex datasets across multiple systems and translates them into actionable dashboards, KPI reports, and analyses that support commercial decision-making.

The position also provides reporting and analytics support across Sales Operations, Customer Service, Rebates, and Accounts Receivable, ensuring visibility into commercial performance and financial outcomes.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Analytics, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field.

  • 3–5+ years of experience in sales operations, business analysis, or a related role.

  • Experience managing and analyzing large datasets across multiple systems.

  • Strong proficiency in:

    • SQL for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.

    • Power BI for dashboard development and KPI reporting.

    • SaaS CRM platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, or similar systems.

    • SAP Business Warehouse.

    • Microsoft SharePoint, Power Automate, and Teams.

  • Experience supporting sales compensation, commission processing, and operational reporting.

  • Experience with enterprise KPI frameworks, commercial reporting standards, and reporting automation.

  • Experience in medical device, healthcare, or other regulated commercial environments preferred.

  • Exposure to Customer Service, Rebates, or Accounts Receivable reporting and analytics.

  • Familiarity with data governance and reporting best practices.

  • Experience with AS400 query languages, such as DB2/IBM i SQL, is a plus.

  • Reliable attendance and flexibility to accommodate non-standard work hours as needed.

  • Ability to manage job-related stress and maintain productive working relationships.

Job Responsibilities

Data & Analytics

  • Manage and analyze large datasets from CRM, ERP, and other enterprise systems.

  • Develop and maintain SQL queries and data models to support scalable reporting and analysis.

  • Build, maintain, and enhance Power BI dashboards and recurring reports.

  • Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and consistency of reporting data.

  • Translate complex data into actionable insights that support business decisions and performance improvement.

  • Identify trends, discrepancies, and opportunities across commercial and operational datasets.

Sales Operations & Performance Reporting

  • Support territory planning, quota setting, forecasting, and sales performance tracking.

  • Develop and maintain KPIs, dashboards, and reporting metrics across Sales Operations, Customer Service, Rebates, and Accounts Receivable.

  • Maintain and optimize SaaS CRM platforms to support data quality and usability.

  • Improve operational workflows through documentation, standardization, and automation.

  • Use SharePoint and Microsoft Teams to manage reporting content, documentation, and collaboration.

  • Prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting packages for leadership.

Sales Compensation & Commission Analysis

  • Support sales compensation plan modeling, administration, and analysis.

  • Validate commission calculations, investigate discrepancies, and support resolution of payout issues.

  • Analyze compensation trends and plan effectiveness to ensure alignment with performance goals.

  • Support monthly and quarterly commission processing and reporting.

  • Assist with annual planning activities, including quota and target development.

Rebates & Accounts Receivable Support

  • Collaborate with team members and other departments to research and resolve rebate and sales-tracing issues.

  • Identify recurring or systemic issues and communicate findings to department management.

  • Support rebate administration processes, reporting, and operational improvements.

  • Assist with training new Rebate Coordinators and cross-training existing employees on rebate administration systems and processes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Special Projects

  • Partner with Sales, Finance, Customer Service, IT, and other commercial teams to align data, systems, and reporting.

  • Communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Provide analytical support for cross-functional initiatives and track project deliverables.

  • Participate in special projects, including system testing and coordination with other departments.

  • Collaborate with department management to develop relevant testing scenarios and support system improvements.

  • Perform other duties and projects as assigned.

Professional Competencies

  • Problem-Solving: Investigates issues, analyzes information, evaluates alternatives, and develops effective solutions.

  • Communication: Communicates clearly and professionally, listens actively, presents numerical data effectively, and prepares accurate written reports.

  • Customer Service: Responds promptly to requests, manages challenging situations professionally, and follows through on commitments.

  • Planning & Organization: Prioritizes tasks, manages time effectively, establishes objectives, and develops realistic action plans.

  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Demonstrates creativity, identifies opportunities for improvement, and develops practical solutions.

  • Teamwork: Collaborates effectively across departments and maintains productive working relationships.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

  • Approximately 75% of the workday is spent seated in an office environment using a computer and telephone.

  • Approximately 25% of the workday involves interacting with employees and management through meetings and other collaborative activities.

  • Requires mobility and availability to attend meetings as needed.

  • Works in a smoke-free office environment with frequent interaction with customers and employees at corporate headquarters.

job.title: PAC Operations and Compliance Consultant
job.description:
Political Action Committee (Client) Operations & Compliance Specialist

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Political Action Committee (Client) Operations & Compliance Specialist to oversee operational, financial, administrative, and compliance activities associated with corporate political contributions and Political Action Committee operations.

This position plays a critical role in managing political contribution processing, regulatory reporting, financial controls, vendor contracts, audit documentation, and internal compliance procedures.

The specialist will coordinate with internal legal, finance, procurement, payroll, and executive leadership teams, as well as international disbursement operations, to ensure accurate and timely processing of political contributions in accordance with federal and state regulations and internal company policies.

The ideal candidate will have strong financial administration, regulatory compliance, documentation management, and cross-functional coordination experience.

Key Responsibilities

Client & Corporate Contributions Management

  • Process, document, and track Client and corporate contribution checks in compliance with federal, state, and company guidelines.

  • Review and interpret corporate contribution requests, including applicable pay-to-play laws and contributions to 527 political organizations.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact with international disbursement teams regarding check issuance, processing, and supporting documentation.

  • Maintain accurate records of contribution check numbers, approvals, and transactions to prevent skipped, duplicate, or unauthorized checks.

  • Track and manage special Client and corporate contribution budget increases throughout the year.

  • Ensure proper documentation and approval of all contribution requests.

Documentation, Records Management & Compliance

  • Maintain physical and electronic Client records in accordance with corporate records retention policies.

  • Administer records management systems and coordinate annual document destruction notifications.

  • Maintain documentation supporting Senior Vice President (SVP) approvals for Client and corporate contribution requests.

  • Manage and maintain approximately 20 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) supporting regulatory compliance and internal controls.

  • Ensure documentation remains current, accurate, and audit-ready.

  • Process and follow up on outstanding contribution checks on a monthly basis.

  • Support internal audits, regulatory reviews, and compliance assessments.

Banking Operations & Positive Pay Administration

  • Manage Positive Pay exceptions and banking file uploads for multiple corporate bank accounts, including federal and state-specific accounts.

  • Coordinate weekly uploads of Client contribution checks to ensure accurate payment processing.

  • Investigate and resolve Positive Pay exceptions and discrepancies.

  • Maintain financial controls designed to prevent fraud and unauthorized transactions.

  • Ensure banking activities comply with established financial procedures and regulatory requirements.

Regulatory Reporting & Legal Coordination

  • Partner with corporate legal counsel and executive leadership to collect political contribution information for required regulatory reports.

  • Coordinate the preparation of the Maryland Business Entity Report, including collection of personal contribution data from executive leadership.

  • Prepare and support the submission of annual and mid-year political contributions reports.

  • Coordinate with internal communications and compliance teams to publish and update political contribution reporting information on corporate websites.

  • Manage website content updates through established change request processes.

  • Provide accurate political contribution data for internal reporting, public disclosures, and regulatory filings.

  • Maintain supporting documentation for compliance and audit purposes.

Client Membership & Payroll Coordination

  • Maintain and update Client membership records and related databases.

  • Coordinate payroll deduction information and resolve membership or contribution discrepancies.

  • Manage exceptions requiring manual payroll uploads for state-specific Client accounts.

  • Temporarily suspend or reactivate automated payroll processes in Workday as needed.

  • Perform manual contribution data uploads into Client management systems such as Quorum.

  • Ensure accurate reconciliation and documentation of payroll-related Client contributions.

Vendor & Contract Management

  • Coordinate vendor contract reviews to ensure compliance with internal procurement and legal requirements.

  • Partner with Procurement to facilitate contract renewals, purchase orders, and vendor payments.

  • Maintain accurate vendor records, agreements, and supporting documentation.

  • Utilize enterprise procurement and financial systems, including SAP and Fiori, to process purchasing and payment activities.

  • Monitor vendor agreements and ensure timely completion of required administrative processes.

Client Strategy, Communications & Campaign Support

  • Support Client strategy development and operational initiatives.

  • Coordinate with internal Client engagement networks to distribute updated resources, materials, and communications.

  • Assist with planning and execution of Client solicitation and employee engagement campaigns.

  • Support the development of campaign communications and incentive gift strategies.

  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to improve Client participation, operational efficiency, and compliance processes.

Notary & General Administrative Support

  • Provide notary services for Client-related documentation as required.

  • Maintain confidential corporate and employee contribution information.

  • Assist with special projects, compliance initiatives, and additional administrative responsibilities as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Experience & Knowledge

  • Experience in financial operations, compliance administration, corporate contributions, regulatory reporting, or a related field.

  • Familiarity with U.S. political contribution regulations, including federal and state requirements.

  • Understanding of corporate compliance procedures, internal controls, and records retention requirements.

  • Experience managing confidential financial information and regulatory documentation.

  • Ability to coordinate multiple administrative and compliance processes simultaneously.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

  • Experience with enterprise financial and administrative systems such as:

    • SAP

    • Workday

    • Fiori

    • Procurement and purchase order management systems

  • Ability to maintain spreadsheets, databases, financial records, and compliance reports.

  • Experience with electronic document management and recordkeeping systems.

Core Competencies

  • Strong organizational and project management skills.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and documentation accuracy.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet strict reporting deadlines.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and reconciliation skills.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Legal, Finance, Payroll, Procurement, and executive leadership.

  • High level of professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.

  • Ability to interpret policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience supporting a Political Action Committee (Client) or corporate political contributions program.

  • Knowledge of campaign finance regulations, pay-to-play restrictions, and 527 organizations.

  • Experience with Positive Pay, banking reconciliations, or check disbursement processes.

  • Familiarity with Quorum or similar Client management software.

  • Experience coordinating regulatory filings and political contribution disclosures.

  • Experience developing, maintaining, or auditing SOPs.

  • Vendor contract administration and procurement experience.

  • Notary Public certification preferred; may be required depending on assignment needs.

Key Areas of Focus

  • Political Action Committee administration and contribution processing

  • Campaign finance compliance and regulatory reporting

  • Financial controls, Positive Pay, and banking operations

  • Records retention, documentation management, and audit readiness

  • Payroll coordination and Client membership administration

  • SAP, Workday, Fiori, and Quorum

  • Vendor contracts, procurement, and purchase order processing

  • Cross-functional coordination with Legal, Finance, and executive leadership

job.title: CNC Machinist - Aerospace
job.description:
Location: Tulsa, OK  |  Type: Full-Time  |  Pay: $22.00–$27.00/hr

An established aerospace manufacturing company in the Tulsa area is seeking an experienced CNC Machinist to join its production team.

This position is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining CNC equipment to manufacture precision components according to engineering drawings and quality specifications.

The ideal candidate will have experience working with CNC machinery, strong attention to detail, and the ability to produce accurate, high-quality parts in a manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Set up and operate CNC machines to manufacture precision components.
  • Read and interpret blueprints, engineering drawings, and technical specifications.
  • Perform machine setups, tooling changes, and adjustments to maintain production requirements.
  • Monitor machining operations to ensure parts meet dimensional and quality standards.
  • Inspect finished components using precision measuring instruments, including calipers, micrometers, and gauges.
  • Make necessary machine offsets and adjustments to maintain tolerances.
  • Identify and troubleshoot machining, tooling, and equipment issues.
  • Follow established work instructions, production schedules, and quality procedures.
  • Maintain accurate production and inspection documentation.
  • Perform routine machine maintenance and maintain a clean, organized work area.
  • Work closely with production, quality, and engineering teams to resolve manufacturing challenges.
  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

  • Previous experience operating CNC equipment in a manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints and engineering drawings.
  • Experience using precision measuring instruments.
  • Understanding of machining processes, tooling, feeds, speeds, and machine offsets.
  • Ability to maintain tight tolerances and meet quality standards.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a production team.
  • Good attendance, reliability, and attention to detail.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience setting up CNC mills, lathes, or other precision machining equipment.
  • Familiarity with G-code and M-code.
  • Experience making basic CNC program edits or adjustments.
  • Experience with precision machined components and close-tolerance work.
  • Knowledge of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing).
  • Experience working with metals and other industrial materials.
  • Experience with HAAS controls, Fanuc controls, milling setups, horizontal/vertical machining
  • Familiarity with quality first-article inspection processes and manufacturing documentation.
  • Technical training or certification in machining or manufacturing technology.

Qualified candidates are encouraged to send resumes to staylor@nescoresource.com and/or contact 918.297.0006 to schedule an interview.

job.title: Housekeeping Technician
job.description:
Job Title: Housekeeping Technician
Interview Process: 1 in person interview

The Housekeeping Technician plays a critical role in maintaining a clean, safe, and compliant production environment within a 24/7 manufacturing facility. This position is responsible for planning, scheduling, and executing routine and specialized cleaning activities that support operational efficiency, product quality, and regulatory standards. The ideal candidate is detail oriented, proactive, and comfortable working in a fast paced industrial setting.

Key Responsibilities
Cleaning Planning & Scheduling
Collaborate with departments to develop and maintain daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning schedules for production areas, equipment, and support spaces.
Coordinate cleaning activities around production demands to minimize downtime and ensure continuous operations.
Manage schedules as needed based on production changes, maintenance needs, or audit findings.

Execution of Cleaning Activities
Perform routine and deep cleaning tasks in production areas, including floors, walls, and high touch zones.
Follow established sanitation procedures, including proper chemical handling, dilution, and application.
Operate cleaning equipment such as floor scrubbers, vacuums, pressure washers, and other industrial tools.
Ensure all cleaning tasks meet internal standards, customer expectations, and regulatory requirements (e.g., GMP, OSHA, ISO).
Inspect all containments erected in production areas and report deficiencies to maintenance leadership.

Documentation & Compliance
Complete cleaning logs, checklists, and digital records accurately and on time.
Support internal and external audits by providing documentation and demonstrating compliance with housekeeping standards.
Report any deviations, safety hazards, or equipment issues promptly.
Collaboration & Communication
Work closely with production, maintenance, and quality teams to coordinate cleaning activities.
Work closely with the contracted housekeeping provider and work cross functionally as needed to address facilities cleaning activities for emergency cleaning or special events.
Communicate schedule changes, task completion, and issues to supervisors and team members.
Safety & Continuous Improvement
Follow all safety protocols, including PPE use, chemical safety, and lockout/tagout when required.
Identify opportunities to improve cleaning processes, tools, and efficiency.
Support training of new team members on cleaning procedures and safety practices.

Qualifications
Previous experience in industrial housekeeping, sanitation, or manufacturing environments preferred.
Experience maintaining clean room environments.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Comfortable working in a 24/7 facility with rotating or fixed shifts as assigned.
Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 lbs and perform physical tasks for extended periods.
Basic computer skills for logging activities and accessing schedules.

Work Environment
Fast paced manufacturing setting with exposure to machinery, noise, chemicals, and varying temperatures.
Requires adherence to strict safety and cleanliness standards.
May involve working nights, weekends, or holidays depending on shift assignment.

job.title: Operations Specialist - III (Senior)
job.description:
Role Purpose
The Sprint Operations SME will provide dedicated shop-floor, process operations, and recipe expertise to the Sprint team during the DeltaV software development, testing, and commissioning phases. Working within an Agile/Sprint team structure, this role bridges the gap between software development and daily manufacturing reality.
The successful candidate will ensure that the new Emerson DeltaV automation solution being installed as part of the Fastnet project accurately reflects current and future manufacturing requirements, supports safe and compliant operations, and enables a robust, seamless facility start up.

Key Responsibilities
1. Agile Sprint Team Integration & Collaboration
Active Sprint Participation: Serve as the core Operations representative within DeltaV software development sprint teams, participating in daily stand-ups, sprint planning, backlog grooming, and sprint demonstrations.
Operational Feedback: Provide immediate, practical feedback on process operations, equipment utilization, operator workflows, and physical facility constraints to the development team.
Peer Communication: Act as the primary liaison between the automation development team and the wider Fastnet Operations team translating technical progress and gathering feedback as required.
2. Operational Translation & Requirement Definition
Legacy-to-DeltaV Translation: Translate existing *** DCS functionality, operating practices, and tacit operational knowledge into clear, actionable requirements for DeltaV functional design, configuration, graphics, and equipment modules.
Recipe & Batch Sheet Interpretation: Utilize deep manufacturing and recipe knowledge to interpret batch sheets/EBRs and operational needs, converting them into optimized DeltaV phases, recipes, control modules, and sequential operations.
Graphics Input: Inform the design of intuitive operator interfaces, control graphics, and navigation paths to ensure ease of use, minimize human error, and streamline physical operator workflows.
3. Design Review, Testing, and Commissioning Support
Document Review & Approval: Review and approve Functional Design Specifications (FDS), Software Requirement Specifications (SRS), design documents, test scripts, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure operational accuracy.
Testing Execution Support: Support software design reviews, sprint demonstrations, internal design reviews, Software Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Developer System Acceptance Testing (DSAT), commissioning, Sequence of Operation testing, and integrated system testing.
Risk & Gap Identification: Proactively identify functional gaps, overlooked operational elements, safety risks, or unintended procedural consequences in the proposed DeltaV design, collaborating with DMO, DMMD, CDS, CQV, Quality, Engineering, and vendor partners to resolve them.
4. Operational & Safety Philosophy Input
Access & Intervention: Provide operator-centric input on operator access philosophy, manual intervention requirements, and abnormal situation handling.
Alarm & Interlock Management: Inform alarm response requirements, interlock philosophy, and equipment module operating parameters to ensure a safe, high-performing operating window.

Safety Reviews: Participate actively in Process Hazard Analyses (PHA), Layers of Protection Analyses (LOPA), CHAZOPs, design safety reviews, 3D model reviews and final system handovers.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Accuracy of Requirements: Minimal gaps or functional changes required during late-stage testing (FAT/SAT/Commissioning) due to complete operational translation during sprint cycles.
Sprint Velocity Support: Timely turnaround of document reviews, clarifications, and user feedback within sprint boundaries to maintain the development schedule.
Transition Readiness: Successful preparation of operating procedures and training inputs to ensure operators are ready to transition to DeltaV controls smoothly enabling RFT facility start-up.

Qualifications & Experience
Required:
Operational Expertise: Significant hands-on experience in biopharmaceutical drug substance and SDI operations, with a deep understanding of process equipment, utility systems, and facility layouts.
Legacy System Knowledge: Strong familiarity with legacy API/SDI control system functionality and the ability to interpret existing operating sequences.
Recipe Management Experience: Prior experience in recipe creation, batch sheet/EBR execution, and operational sequence design under computerized control environments.
Commercial supply Experience: Hands-on experience navigating the commercial supply phase of biopharmaceutical manufacturing, ensuring compliance with GMP and regulatory standards.
Communication & Collaboration: Excellent communication skills with a proven track record of effectively translating complex operational procedures to engineering/automation teams and vice versa.

Preferred:
DeltaV Experience: Familiarity with Emerson DeltaV system navigation, batch execution, or previous exposure to DeltaV system migration projects.
Agile Exposure: Prior experience working in an Agile development environment (Scrum/Kanban), participating in sprint-based delivery.
CQV Experience: Active participation in Commissioning, Qualification, and Validation (CQV) activities in a regulated pharmaceutical facility.

job.title: Maintenance Tech I
job.description:
Industrial Maintenance Technician – Automation & Robotics

Shift Options:

  • 2nd Shift: Sunday–Thursday, 2:00 PM–10:30 PM

  • 3rd Shift: Sunday–Thursday, 11:00 PM–7:30 AM

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Industrial Maintenance Technician to maintain, troubleshoot, repair, and perform preventive maintenance on industrial production equipment, conveyors, automation systems, and robotics. This position plays an important role in ensuring equipment reliability, minimizing production downtime, and maintaining a safe and efficient manufacturing environment.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience troubleshooting mechanical, electrical, and automated equipment, including PLC-controlled systems, and can work independently while collaborating with other maintenance personnel.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform preventive maintenance, routine inspections, adjustments, and repairs on conveyors, automated production equipment, robotics, and related machinery.

  • Troubleshoot equipment malfunctions and identify mechanical, electrical, and controls-related issues.

  • Diagnose and resolve equipment faults involving PLC systems, sensors, inputs, outputs, and related components.

  • Assemble, test, and inspect equipment to verify proper operation and production readiness.

  • Investigate equipment failures, analyze production downtime, and assist with root cause analysis and corrective actions.

  • Document maintenance activities, equipment issues, repairs, and work orders in computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS).

  • Maintain accurate maintenance logs and operating records for production and facility equipment.

  • Collaborate with maintenance mechanics, operations, engineering, and other team members to resolve equipment issues.

  • Assist with general facility maintenance, including lighting, doors, minor plumbing, carpentry, HVAC-related tasks, and other building repairs as needed.

  • Follow established safety procedures, including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Arc Flash precautions, and proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

  • Support additional maintenance projects, equipment installations, and other operational needs as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience maintaining or repairing conveyors, automation systems, robotics, or related industrial equipment.

  • Fundamental understanding of mechanical and electrical equipment.

  • Experience troubleshooting PLC-controlled equipment, including inputs, outputs, and basic control logic.

  • Ability to perform preventive maintenance, diagnose equipment failures, and complete repairs safely and effectively.

  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and electronic maintenance documentation.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

  • Willingness to learn new equipment, work overtime as needed, and travel up to 10% for business purposes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering Technology, HVAC, or a related field.

  • Completion of a maintenance apprenticeship or relevant trade certification.

  • Experience with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS).

  • Experience in facility or building maintenance within a large industrial or commercial facility.

  • Familiarity with industrial safety standards and equipment reliability practices.

Physical & Work Environment Requirements

  • Ability to stand and move for extended periods during a shift.

  • Ability to frequently lift and carry up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift up to 75 pounds.

  • Ability to bend, twist, reach, climb ladders and stairs, work at heights, and perform overhead maintenance tasks.

  • Ability to work safely around industrial machinery and follow all required safety procedures.

  • Willingness to operate material-handling equipment, such as a forklift, when required.

  • Availability for overtime and on-call requests as needed.

Work Schedule

This position offers second- or third-shift scheduling, Sunday through Thursday. Candidates must be comfortable working the assigned shift and adjusting their schedules as operational needs require.

Qualified candidates with industrial maintenance, automation, robotics, conveyor, and PLC troubleshooting experience are encouraged to apply.

job.title: Tool Design Engineer - (Aerospace)
job.description:
Description:
Designs industrial machinery and equipment, tools, dies, gauges, jigs, fixtures, and machine attachments required for production or experimental use, considering such factors as accessibility, economy, mobility, and performance requirements.
Complete understanding and wide application of technical principles, theories and concepts, in the field.
Independently determines and develops approach to solutions.
Provides technical solutions to a wide range of difficult problems.
May use CAD/CAM to design tools.

You will be the Tool Design Engineer for the Missiles and Fire Control team in Ocala. Our team is responsible for designing dies, gauges, jigs, fixtures, prototype models, and robotics end-of-arm tooling for production or experimental purposes.

What You Will Be Doing
As the Tool Design Engineer, you will be responsible for utilizing 3D modeling software to conceptualize, create, and integrate industrial machinery, equipment, and tools. Your responsibilities will include:

Designing dies, gauges, jigs, fixtures, harness boards, prototype models, and robotics end-of-arm tooling for production or experimental purposes.
Accounting for various factors such as accessibility, ergonomics, safety, economy, mobility, and performance requirements while developing solutions.
Designs, develops and implements industrial machinery and equipment, tools, dies, gauges, jigs, fixtures, prototype model production and machine attachments required for production or experimental use, considering such factors as accessibility, economy, mobility, and performance requirements.
May use CAD/CAM to design tools.

Required Experience:
A Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering field.
• Candidate must have at least 6 years of experience with 3D modeling software, such as SolidWorks, or CREO.
• Candidate must have at least 6 years of experience with CAD/CAM systems (Creo) & PLM system (Windchill)
• Candidate must have at least 6 years of experience with Harness Board design
• Strong understanding of engineering principles, manufacturing processes, and materials.
• This position is located at a facility that requires special access, therefore the selected candidate must be a U.S. Citizen.

Desired Skills:
• Ability to analyze and solve complex engineering problems.
• Familiarity with CNC machining, fabrication, and assembly techniques.
• Knowledge of safety regulations and industry standards.
• Strong communication and teamwork skills.
• Experience in managing projects, schedules, and resources.
• Knowledge of robotics and automation systems.
• Understanding of Lean manufacturing principles and practices.

job.title: Recruiter
job.description:
Recruiter – Talent Acquisition

Position Overview

We are seeking a motivated and organized Recruiter to support full-cycle recruiting and talent acquisition activities across assigned business areas.

This position will partner closely with hiring managers, HR Business Partners, and internal stakeholders to identify hiring needs, develop sourcing strategies, screen and evaluate candidates, coordinate interviews, and facilitate hiring decisions.

The ideal candidate will have strong communication skills, experience managing multiple requisitions, and the ability to deliver an efficient, compliant, and positive recruiting experience for both candidates and hiring managers.

Position Details

  • Location: Ogden, UT

  • Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite

  • Shift: 1st Shift

  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, 7:00 AM – 4:30 PM (flexible)

  • Assignment Duration: Approximately 1 year, with the possibility of extension

Key Responsibilities

Full-Cycle Recruiting & Talent Acquisition

  • Manage full-cycle recruiting activities from requisition intake through offer acceptance.

  • Partner with hiring managers to understand staffing needs, position requirements, qualifications, and hiring timelines.

  • Review, revise, and standardize job descriptions to accurately reflect business needs and recruiting best practices.

  • Develop and execute recruiting strategies to identify and attract qualified candidates.

  • Manage multiple open requisitions while ensuring timely candidate submissions and hiring decisions.

  • Serve as a trusted recruiting partner to hiring managers and HR Business Partners.

Candidate Sourcing & Talent Pipeline Development

  • Proactively source candidates through multiple recruiting channels, including:

    • LinkedIn Recruiter

    • Boolean search techniques

    • Internal and external job boards

    • Professional networking

    • Employee referrals

    • Social media platforms

    • Industry-specific recruiting resources

  • Develop and maintain talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs.

  • Identify qualified candidates through resume searches, networking, and direct outreach.

  • Support employer branding initiatives to attract high-quality talent.

Candidate Screening & Assessment

  • Review resumes and applications to evaluate candidate qualifications.

  • Conduct initial phone and video interviews to assess skills, experience, qualifications, and interest.

  • Evaluate candidates against position requirements and hiring manager expectations.

  • Present qualified candidates to hiring managers with clear summaries and recommendations.

  • Maintain consistent communication with candidates throughout the recruiting process.

  • Provide timely updates regarding interview schedules, feedback, hiring decisions, and next steps.

Interview Coordination & Hiring Support

  • Coordinate interview scheduling between candidates and hiring teams.

  • Prepare interviewers with appropriate interview guides, evaluation forms, and candidate information.

  • Collect and track interviewer feedback.

  • Facilitate interview debriefs and support hiring decisions.

  • Assist with offer development, offer extensions, and candidate negotiations.

  • Manage offer acceptance and decline communications.

  • Partner with HR and onboarding teams to support a smooth transition from candidate selection to new hire onboarding.

Applicant Tracking Systems & Recruiting Reporting

  • Maintain accurate candidate, requisition, and recruiting activity records within the Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and HRIS platforms.

  • Ensure recruiting documentation is complete, accurate, and current.

  • Generate and maintain recruiting reports and pipeline metrics, including:

    • Time-to-fill

    • Candidate pipeline activity

    • Sourcing effectiveness

    • Candidate conversion rates

    • Recruiting progress and requisition status

  • Utilize recruiting data to identify opportunities for process improvement.

Recruiting Compliance & Process Improvement

  • Ensure recruiting activities comply with applicable federal, state, and local employment laws.

  • Follow established hiring policies, procedures, and documentation requirements.

  • Maintain confidentiality of candidate information and hiring decisions.

  • Support diversity, equity, and inclusion recruiting initiatives.

  • Recommend improvements to sourcing strategies, recruiting workflows, and candidate engagement processes.

  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance recruiting efficiency and reduce time-to-hire.

Additional Responsibilities

As needed, the Recruiter may also:

  • Partner with HR teams on onboarding coordination and first-day preparation.

  • Assist with recruiting events, career fairs, and campus recruiting activities.

  • Support employer branding and industry outreach initiatives.

  • Participate in workforce planning and recruiting-related reporting projects.

  • Assist with occasional HR generalist tasks and administrative projects.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field preferred.

  • Candidates currently attending college are eligible for consideration and may be submitted.

Experience

  • 3+ years of recruiting or talent acquisition experience preferred, either within corporate recruiting or staffing agency environments.

  • Experience managing full-cycle recruiting activities.

  • Ability to manage multiple requisitions, priorities, and hiring deadlines.

  • Experience partnering directly with hiring managers and HR stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated ability to source, screen, and assess candidates effectively.

job.title: Equipment Installation Lead
job.description:
Position Title: Equipment Installation Lead

Location: Newton, NC

Schedule: M-F: 8-5, Occasional OT


Position Scope:
The Equipment Installation Lead is a senior technical role responsible for directing and performing complex mechanical equipment installations. This position provides on-site leadership, technical expertise, and project coordination to ensure installations are completed safely, on schedule, and in accordance with engineering specifications, quality standards, and customer requirements. The Lead Technician also serves as a subject matter expert and mentors junior technicians.

• This Engineering Project role focuses on capacity expansion and the mechanical installation and debugging of associated production lines.

• Lead or participate in manufacturing engineering projects and teams involving capacity installations, equipment debugging, and preparation of production lines and related components for Operations acceptance.

• Apply advanced mechanical expertise to identify root causes and implement robust, production-ready solutions during line installations and debugging.

• Apply knowledge of mechanical and electrical engineering, machining, and design processes to improve equipment and manufacturing performance.

• Lead and support project planning and execution to provide timely, error-free mechanical support for multi-line equipment installations.

• Work effectively with vendors and suppliers to resolve technical issues while protecting project scope, schedule, and cost.

• Collaborate across functional groups and apply best practices to achieve daily project goals.

• Interpret and work from detailed engineering drawings, schematics, blueprints, and installation manuals.

• Perform advanced mechanical work, including rigging, leveling, precision alignment, torquing, piping, and mechanical integration.

• Troubleshoot and resolve installation problems, equipment malfunctions, and mechanical interferences.

• Verify that installations comply with OEM specifications, safety codes, and quality standards.


Team Leadership & Coordination

  • Serve as the on-site Lead Technician, directing the daily work of installation crews and subcontractors.
  • Assign tasks, track progress, and ensure labor and resources are used efficiently.
  • Train and mentor junior technicians through hands-on guidance and technical instruction.
  • Act as the primary technical liaison among field teams, engineers, project managers, and customers.

Quality & Documentation

  • Perform inspections and quality checks throughout installation.
  • Complete installation reports, checklists, punch lists, and as-built documentation.
  • Support equipment testing, startup, and customer acceptance.

Project Support

  • Support installation planning, sequencing, and scheduling.
  • Coordinate the materials, tools, and equipment required for installation.
  • Promote continuous improvement and best practices in installation methods.

Daily Responsibilities:

  • Maintain safe work practices and promptly report hazardous conditions or unsafe behaviors to the project team.
  • Lead installation and debugging activities to meet milestones and schedules for successful capacity expansions.
  • Design and implement mechanical solutions and process changes that improve manufacturing equipment capability.
  • Resolve mechanical and process issues through data analysis, experience, and collaboration with subject matter experts.
  • Manage spare-parts identification and storeroom entry based on supplier or engineering recommendations, accounting for available inventory across both plants.
  • Create and maintain engineering and operations documentation.
  • Train operations personnel on equipment and process changes.
  • Perform advanced troubleshooting, diagnosis, and repair of mechanical systems and equipment, including pumps, motors, conveyors, hydraulics, and pneumatics.
  • Align, test, and calibrate mechanical systems after installation.
  • Diagnose complex mechanical failures and recommend effective solutions.
  • Use blueprints, schematics, and technical manuals to support troubleshooting and repairs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, efficiency, and safety.
  • Partner with other departments to implement process improvements.

Qualifications

Required Education:

  • Associate degree.
  • A high school diploma may be accepted with substantial hands-on experience.

Required Experience:

  • At least three years of experience installing new equipment in a manufacturing environment; startup experience is preferred.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, changing environment.
  • Strong knowledge of mechanical systems, industrial equipment, and installation methods.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation.
  • Experience leading crews in industrial, manufacturing, semiconductor, energy, or similar environments.

Required Skills:

  • Ability to quickly learn new technologies and processes.
  • Strong technical foundation and mechanical engineering skills.
  • Ability to independently prioritize and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced manufacturing installation environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Expertise in pneumatics, bearings, gear systems, conveyors, and other mechanical systems.
  • Ability to interpret technical drawings, blueprints, and schematics.
  • Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and diagnostic equipment.
  • Strong problem-solving, analytical, and critical-thinking abilities.
  • Knowledge of industrial safety regulations and practices.
  • Basic computer skills for recordkeeping and use of computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS).

Certifications:

  • Mechatronics trade credentials are highly preferred.
  • Relevant mechanical or industrial certifications, such as Millwright, or Welding, are a plus.

Desired Skills:

  • Strong leadership skills
  • Hands-on experience with commercial manufacturing equipment.
  • Project leadership or management experience, including milestone management and budget accountability.
  • Experience managing vendors and suppliers on-site and remotely.
  • CAD experience.
  • Experience with Maximo, or maintenance leadership.
  • Detail-oriented and able to work with limited supervision.

Soft Skills:

  • Leadership experience in technical project management.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively within a team.
  • Ability to allocate and supervise resources to meet aggressive project milestones, schedules, specifications, and budgets.
  • Ability to shift priorities quickly.
  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Travel Requirements:

  • Travel between project sites in Newton and Hickory, North Carolina.

Work Schedule and Flexibility:

  • Standard schedule is 40 hours per week, with overtime expected. Project demands may require periodic off-hours coverage to complete work and coordinate with team members.

job.title: Tooling and Gage Designer
job.description:
Tooling & Gaging Design Engineer

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented Tooling and Gaging Designer to support precision manufacturing operations. This individual will be responsible for developing and maintaining custom tooling, production fixtures, and measurement systems used in manufacturing and quality inspection.

Working in partnership with engineering, production, and quality teams, the successful candidate will translate technical requirements into practical design solutions that improve manufacturing processes, maintain product consistency, and support the introduction of new products. This role also contributes to ongoing production support, process optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop custom tooling, workholding fixtures, inspection gages, and related equipment for precision manufacturing applications.

  • Produce and maintain 3D CAD models, technical drawings, and supporting engineering documentation.

  • Develop tooling and inspection solutions for new product launches and changes to existing manufacturing processes.

  • Translate engineering specifications, conceptual sketches, production requirements, and other technical inputs into functional designs.

  • Evaluate and improve existing tooling and gaging systems to enhance reliability, accuracy, and production efficiency.

  • Prepare and maintain inspection equipment documentation, usage instructions, design records, and technical procedures.

  • Troubleshoot manufacturing and measurement challenges, recommend corrective actions, and implement design improvements.

  • Establish consistent design practices and technical standards for tooling and gaging used across manufacturing operations.

  • Review engineering drawings and design documentation to verify accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable standards.

  • Maintain tooling databases, inventory records, and documentation to support equipment tracking and availability.

  • Coordinate tooling inventory organization and assist with the development and maintenance of departmental procedures.

  • Partner with manufacturing, quality, product engineering, and operations personnel to address technical issues and production needs.

  • Participate in Lean Manufacturing, process improvement, and other operational excellence initiatives.

  • Interpret engineering drawings, customer requirements, technical specifications, and applicable industry standards.

  • Identify drawing and documentation requirements for new products, design revisions, and specialized manufacturing applications.

  • Communicate design concepts, technical recommendations, and engineering findings clearly through written documentation and verbal discussions.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Mechanical Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Engineering Technology, Quality Engineering Technology, or a related technical field; equivalent relevant education and experience will also be considered.

  • At least three years of experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment.

  • Background in precision manufacturing, machining, or inspection processes is preferred.

  • Experience in bearing manufacturing or a related mechanical component industry is beneficial.

Required Knowledge and Skills

  • Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling and mechanical drawing creation; experience with SolidWorks or comparable design software is preferred.

  • Familiarity with product data management systems and engineering document control.

  • Working knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), mechanical drafting, and design standards.

  • Understanding of precision measurement equipment, inspection methods, and gaging principles.

  • Familiarity with Statistical Process Control (SPC) and its application in manufacturing.

  • Knowledge of machining and finishing processes, including turning, grinding, assembly, and dimensional inspection.

  • Awareness of quality management system requirements, such as ISO 9001 and AS9100.

  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, engineering specifications, and industry standards.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

  • Experience with tooling or equipment inventory management software is preferred.

  • Strong analytical thinking, organization, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across multiple departments.

Compensation will depend on the candidate's relevant experience, education, technical capabilities, and other job-related considerations. The stated range reflects the anticipated compensation for this position in Connecticut.

job.title: Network Consultant
job.description:
Nesco Data Center is seeking a Network Consultant in the Greater Bethesda MD area. This is part-time position working Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 8:30am - 4:30pm. 

Job Description: Senior Network Consultant

Position Overview

The Senior Network Consultant provides scheduled, proactive technical consulting services to optimize, maintain, secure, and document network infrastructure and supported systems in alignment with evolving business and technology objectives. This role focuses on preventative maintenance, network performance optimization, systems administration, security configuration, troubleshooting, and technical documentation.

The consultant works with designated operational leaders and technical stakeholders to prioritize initiatives, maintain system stability, identify recurring issues, and recommend improvements to the supported technology environment.

Key Responsibilities and Services

  1. Network Switching and Virtualization: Configure and optimize physical and virtual switches, including port security, VLANs, IP helper settings, link aggregation, and other supported equipment features.

  2. Firewall and VPN Administration: Configure, troubleshoot, and optimize firewall rules, VPNs, network address translation (NAT), port forwarding, and access control lists.

  3. Storage Administration: Administer and optimize supported storage area network (SAN) infrastructure.

  4. Routing and Edge Devices: Configure and maintain routing functionality on supported edge devices.

  5. Network Performance Management: Monitor network performance, analyze trends, identify bottlenecks, and recommend or implement appropriate optimizations.

  6. UPS Monitoring and Management: Monitor UPS health and capacity, configure centralized management, and maintain shutdown policies for supported systems and devices.

  7. Firmware and Security Maintenance: Apply approved firmware updates, security patches, service packs, and zero-day security updates to supported equipment and systems.

  8. Redundancy and Contingency Testing: Periodically test failover capabilities, redundancies, and other established continuity safeguards.

  9. Credential Management: Periodically rotate credentials on supported equipment in accordance with established security practices.

  10. Directory Services Administration: Maintain cloud-based and on-premises directory services, including object, organizational unit, and group policy additions, modifications, and deletions.

  11. Email Administration: Perform email account provisioning, modifications, and deactivation.

  12. Core Systems Administration: Troubleshoot and perform minor configuration changes to DNS, DHCP, network printing, and other basic supported infrastructure services.

  13. Printer and Print Services Management: Configure network printers and administer on-premises or cloud-based print services.

  14. Routine System Changes and Optimization: Perform approved configuration changes to improve the performance, security, and reliability of supported servers, services, and systems.

  15. Technical Documentation: Maintain accurate documentation of supported systems, configurations, and changes performed.

  16. Network Diagrams and Visualizations: Create and maintain custom infrastructure diagrams to supplement automated documentation and assist technical personnel with troubleshooting and ongoing maintenance.

  17. Software Licensing and Inventory: Track supported server and software inventory, licensing information, and relevant lifecycle dates, including end-of-support and end-of-life milestones.

  18. Problem Management: Identify recurring technical issues, investigate root causes, and recommend corrective actions to improve reliability and reduce repeat incidents.

  19. Public Key Infrastructure and Certificates: Track, renew, and implement public key certificates on supported systems.

  20. Preventative Maintenance and Trend Analysis: Conduct proactive maintenance and analyze system trends at appropriate intervals based on the requirements of each supported technology.

  21. Routine System Updates: Apply approved in-place updates, service packs, and security patches to supported systems, excluding major-version upgrades.

  22. Service Reporting and Recommendations: Produce work reports detailing completed tasks, configuration changes, identified risks, and recommendations for projects or major improvements outside the defined service scope.

  23. Backup Integrity Testing: Perform test restores to validate the integrity and recoverability of backups for supported systems.

  24. Data Restoration Assistance: Assist with restoring data to supported systems following accidental deletion or corruption, using an approved available backup solution.

  25. Operational Coordination: Communicate with operational leadership to provide input on technical initiatives, task prioritization, maintenance activities, and recommended improvements. Use the designated IT service management platform when applicable.

Service Scope and Exclusions

The following activities are outside the standard scope of this position unless separately authorized or covered by an additional service agreement:

  1. End-User Support: Direct end-user help desk and desktop support services.

  2. Unsupported Equipment: Support for equipment without an active vendor support agreement.

  3. Unapproved Technologies: Support for software, hardware, or technologies not explicitly identified in the approved technology inventory or service scope.

  4. Unstable Software Releases: Support for systems running software versions that are not considered current, stable, or appropriately supported.

  5. Major Changes and Projects: Changes requiring extensive project management, specialized subject-matter expertise, significant risk mitigation, or resources beyond the capabilities of a qualified generalist may require a separate scope of work.

  6. New System Configuration: Initial configuration, deployment, or implementation of new systems.

  7. Third-Party Changes: Documentation updates for changes made by other vendors or to equipment and systems outside the defined support scope.

  8. Network Hardware Inventory: Tracking licenses and inventory for networking hardware.

  9. Database Administration: Database administration, maintenance, and specialized database management.

  10. Training: Formal training for end users or other organizational personnel.

  11. Major Version Upgrades: Major operating system, application, or platform upgrades. These may require a separately defined project scope.

  12. Backup Management: Ongoing backup administration and backup-service maintenance are excluded unless specifically included under a separate backup service agreement. The consultant may assist with backup

job.title: CMM Programmer - Aerospace
job.description:
Location: Tulsa, OK  |  Type: Full-Time  |  Pay: $23.00–$30.00/hr
We are seeking a dynamic CMM Programmer/Operator to join a local aerospace manufacturing team. This position is responsible for supporting its quality and inspections operations. This position will be responsible for developing and executing Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) programs, inspecting precision-manufactured components, and ensuring products meet engineering specifications and quality standards.
The ideal candidate will have a strong background in dimensional inspection, CMM programming, blueprint interpretation, and precision measurement within a manufacturing environment.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Program CMMs (Zeiss, Hexagon, Mitutoyo, or similar) using PC-DMIS, Calypso, MODUS, or equivalent software.
  • Interpret engineering drawings, 3D CAD models, and GD&T per ASME Y14.5 to create accurate inspection plans.
  • Develop and import CAD-based, offline, and manual CMM programs for new and existing part numbers.
  • Design and select fixtures, probe configurations, styli, and qualification strategies for complex aerospace geometries.
  • Verify and prove out programs on the machine, optimizing for cycle time, accuracy, and repeatability.
  • Perform first article inspections (FAI) per AS9102 and generate complete, accurate FAI reports.
  • Create and maintain inspection reports, data collection plans, and measurement documentation.
  • Maintain CMM calibration, verification, and routine maintenance records in compliance with ISO 10360 and company procedures.
  • Revise programs in response to engineering change orders (ECOs) and drawing revisions, maintaining strict revision control.
  • Follow AS9100, customer flow-down requirements, and internal quality management system procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned
Required Qualifications
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum of two years of quality inspection experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation
  • Experience using precision measuring instruments and inspection equipment
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office
  • Excellent communication and problem-solving abilities
  • Experience with Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM)
Preferred Qualifications
  • 5+ years of CMM programming experience on aerospace components.
  • Experience with 5-axis CMM, scanning probes, and multi-sensor systems.
  • Experience inspecting turbine components, structural machined parts, castings, forgings, or sheet metal assemblies.
  • Certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Technician (CQT), Certified Quality Inspector (CQI), or Certified Mechanical Inspector (CMI).
  • Familiarity with SPC software, Minitab, or QMS tools such as ERP and MES systems.
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methods.
  • Experience in precision manufacturing, metal fabrication, machining, industrial equipment, or highly regulated manufacturing environments
  • Working knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T)
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001, AS9102, or similar quality management systems
  • Experience performing first article, in-process, and final inspections
  • Ability to program a CMM independently

job.title: Quality Assurance Specialist
job.description:
Quality Assurance & Quality Control Specialist

Position Summary
The Quality Assurance & Quality Control Specialist plays a critical role in ensuring product quality, regulatory compliance, and manufacturing excellence throughout the production process. This position is responsible for maintaining and improving quality systems, performing dimensional and functional inspections, supporting testing activities, and driving continuous improvement initiatives. Working closely with engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, and customers, the specialist helps ensure all valves meet company, customer, and industry standards while reducing rework and improving overall product performance.

Location: Troy, NY
Compensation: $70,000 - $90,000

Key Responsibilities

  • Operate and maintain Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) equipment to perform dimensional inspections and verify compliance with engineering drawings and specifications.
  • Maintain calibration records and ensure all measuring and test equipment remain compliant with established quality procedures and standards.
  • Support and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including compliance with ISO 9001 requirements and associated documentation.
  • Conduct internal quality audits and assist with corrective and preventive action (CAPA) initiatives.
  • Perform and support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), customer witness testing, and vendor inspections.
  • Assist with hydrostatic, functional, and performance testing of valves and related assemblies.
  • Coordinate and oversee the shipment of approximately 8–12 valves per week, ensuring all inspection, testing, and documentation requirements are completed prior to release.
  • Review engineering drawings, specifications, procedures, and customer requirements to verify product conformity.
  • Prepare and maintain inspection reports, test reports, quality records, and compliance documentation.
  • Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and suppliers to identify, investigate, and resolve quality-related issues.
  • Lead and support continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, minimizing rework, and improving first-pass yield.
  • Investigate nonconformances and support root cause analysis and corrective action implementation.
  • Promote quality awareness, accountability, and best practices throughout the organization.
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and professional work environment while adhering to company safety policies and procedures.
Qualifications
  • Associate degree or equivalent experience in Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering Technology, or a related field preferred.
  • Experience in quality assurance, quality control, manufacturing inspection, or industrial production environments.
  • Hands-on experience with CMM operation and dimensional inspection methods preferred.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 9001 quality management systems and documentation requirements.
  • Experience conducting or supporting internal quality audits.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and manufacturing documentation.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to effectively interact with customers, suppliers, auditors, and cross-functional teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and electronic quality record systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Willingness to support customer visits, supplier audits, testing activities, and occasional travel as required.

Key Responsibilities

Administrative & Sales Support

  • Prepare, review, and distribute professional correspondence, emails, reports, and other business documents.

  • Assist with organizing and maintaining confidential client information and sales-related documentation.

  • Perform general administrative duties as directed by department leadership.

  • Support sales representatives with administrative tasks to ensure efficient daily operations.

Sales Submission & Workflow Coordination

job.title: Quality Inspector - (Automotive)
job.description:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Job Summary:
The Quality Inspector will check the quality of all products as well as production procedures. The role will be an advocate for quality in our business. The Quality Inspector will ensure that products are made of flawless materials in compliance with customer specifications.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
• Inspect, test and measure materials or products and accurately record inspection and test data. This includes measuring products using rulers, calipers, gauges, coordinate measuring machines (CMM), thread gauges, gauge pins, optical comparator, surface testers, height gauges or micrometers to monitor operations to ensure they meet quality standards.
• Accept or reject finished products including tagging or identifying all products and material that fail to meet specifications.
• Read, interpret, and follow basic blueprints, diagrams, engineering drawings and other written
instruction. This includes understanding and applying Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerance (GD & T) symbology.
• Recommend adjustments to the assembly or production process to improve quality.
• Calibrate or verify test instruments.
• Adhere to all safety procedures and promote continuous improvement.

Education and Experience (required):
• High School diploma or equivalent.
• 1 year of inspection experience with common hand gages or equivalent.

Education and Experience (preferred):
• 1 year of experience programing and operating a Direct Computer Controlled (DCC) CMM.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities (required):
• Knowledge of computers and electronics.
• Ability to calibrate or verify test instruments and keep detailed records.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to interact across multiple departments.
• Proficient computer skills including MS Office.
• Ability to analyze and problem solve with attention to detail.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities (preferred)
• Working knowledge and comprehension of quality standards.
• American Society for Quality (ASQ) certified.
• Ability to work overtime as needed including weekends.

Additional Information:
Direct Reports: None Travel Requirements: 5%
License and Certification Requirements: None

Physical Requirements:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The employee is regularly required to perform physical activities that require significant use of your arms and legs and moving your whole body, such as climbing, lifting, balancing, walking, stooping, standing for extended periods of time and handling of materials. The employee is required to lift up to 50 pounds on a regular basis. The employee is subject to loud noise, dirt, dust, grease, gases and odors and is required to wear personal protective equipment such as safety glasses and ear protection in required area. Typical vision abilities include close up for fine detailed work and computer work, distance vision and ability to focus. Regular and predictable attendance is required.

job.title: Machine Operator I
job.description:
*Contract-to-Hire
*1st shift (MON-FRI; 1st 5a-1:30p)
*2nd shift (MON-FRI; 2nd 1p-9:30p)
*Over time is required depending on business needs.
* Top skill =: CNC Lathe experience
*Interviews required
•High school diploma or GED from an accredited institution
*Physical required

*Work environment: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts and outside weather conditions. The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals; extreme cold; extreme heat; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 
This is not intended as a comprehensive list; it is intended to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed, and may be required to perform additional, position-specific tasks.

Conducts pre-operations inspections to ensure machine is ready to be operated in safe and efficient manner.

Reads and executes daily production schedule as directed by supervisor.

Will measure, mark, and scribe dimensions and reference points on material or work piece as guides for subsequent machining.

Selects, aligns, and secures holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials on machinery.

Calculates and sets controls to regulate machining factors such as speed, feed, coolant flow, and depth and angle of cut.

Starts and observes machine operation to detect malfunctions or out-of-tolerance machining and adjusts machine controls or control media as required and reports problems to supervisor as necessary.

Verifies conformance of finished work piece to specifications and stops production if any part that is detected to be out of specification.

Will confer with Machine Shop Supervisor to resolve machining problems.

Produces daily production reports, inspections and other reports as directed by supervisor.



Must have understanding and knowledge of company procedures and work instructions.

Maintains a safe and organized workstation and follows all company policies and safety procedures.

Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
High school diploma or GED from an accredited institution.
Minimum 1 year of related experience and/or training;
This position is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) which requires U.S. person status.
Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.


Preferred Qualifications
Experience in a manufacturing environment or industrial environment
Experience working with close tolerance practices of +/- .010 or less, in a manufacturing environment.
Understand how to read blueprints, sketches, drawings, manuals, specifications, or sample part to determine dimensions and tolerances of finished work piece, sequence of operations, and setup requirements.

Value: 1st Shift

Must be able to Interview and Train for their 1st day in Auburn Hills

The Schedule is going to be from 6 am to 2:30 p.m. Monday-Friday Weekeneds as needed

Payrate will start at 18 an hour.

The Hi-lo Driver ensures the correct flow, staging, and replenishment of all packaging materials required for the ESS production Process. This role is responsible for unloading packaging materials, moving them to designated line-side locations, supporting line replenishment, and handling empty containers and returns. The  Hi-lo Driver, follows standard operating procedures, performs visual quality checks on packaging components, and promotes overall organization of the warehouse and production floor.
.
ESSENTIAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Receive, move, and stage packaging materials (trays, cartons, foam, pallets, labels).
Deliver the correct packaging materials to the production line.
Store packaging in the correct line-side or warehouse locations using FIFO.
Inspect packaging materials for damage or incorrect items.
Collect leftover packaging from the line and return it to storage areas.
Handle scrap materials safely, including damaged cells or contaminated packaging.
Handle empty pallets, bins, and reusable containers.
Assist with physical inventory by identifying and reporting counts.
Support to Material Specialist / Drop Zone Activities
Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area to ensure good material flow (new, used, returnable, scrap).
Follow all EHS requirements, including PPE and safety rules for battery handling.
Maintain 5S in all packaging areas (cleaning, organizing, labeling).
Other Tasks as assigned.

Working Experience in materials/logistics areas.
Cycle count experience is preferred.
Working Level Knowledge of: Materials and Logistics.
Highly Organized and Detail-Oriented.
Ability to stand, walk, carry light objects, handle parts, reach with hands and arms, lift, push, and pull materials up to 40–50 lbs regularly.
Ability to multitask and work with minimum supervision
Ability to work overtime as business needs dictate.
Ability to travel between manufacturing facilities as required.
Good organization skills to keep packaging areas sorted and clean.
Ability to stand and walk for 8–12 hours per shift.
Frequent bending, reaching, twisting, and handling of materials.
Ability to work in areas with moving equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks).
Flexible and capable of adapting to change, with the ability to follow work instructions.
Basic knowledge of material identification (good, scrap, recyclable).
Ability to safely handle battery components and packaging materials.
Basic understanding of material movement and line-side staging.
Ability to communicate issues clearly to team leads or supervisors.
Basic understanding of safety requirements (PPE, chemical safety, lifting safety).
